This is a task-based fMRI study using an overt verbal fluency (letter-cued word generation) paradigm that requires goal-directed retrieval under rule constraints (phonemic/letter rules), which fits the review's broad definition of problem-solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for controls (healthy adults) and patient groups (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and provides stereotactic coordinates after transformation into Talairach space (I7). Voxelwise, whole-brain results are presented in maps and tables (I9). It is empirical, not ROI-only, and includes within-group task effects in healthy controls, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in I5. The experimental task is theory-of-mind/mental state attribution (belief vs. desire reasoning), not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to reach a solution. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain, group-level task-based fMRI BOLD results with stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates. Thus it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9 but fails I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning (Wason Selection Task) in healthy adult participants (n=21). It examines problem-solving/reasoning processes (goal-directed evaluation and rule-based operations to determine disconfirmation), satisfying the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables), and presents BOLD fMRI results (task-related activations and psychophysiological interaction effective connectivity). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This task uses visuospatial reasoning problems (selecting matching/development figures), which constitute problem-solving under the review’s I5 definition (goal-directed reasoning and rule-based operations). The study used task-based whole-brain fMRI with group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=8) using SPM (I6). It reports stereotactic coordinates/Brodmann areas (Talairach/MNI) in tables/figures (I7), and BOLD-based analyses (I8). Coordinate results are presented in figures/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to between-group/disease comparisons (E4/E5), and this is original empirical data (not E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Note: small sample size and use of selected ROI time-course analyses for some secondary analyses are methodological limitations but do not violate inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks used (finger tapping, verbal fluency/word generation, working memory digit-recognition, and spatial attention reaction-time) do not require goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a previously unknown solution; they are primarily motor, attention, memory, or semantic-retrieval paradigms rather than problem-solving per the provided definition. The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level analysis (I6), stereotactic coordinates reported (I7), BOLD analysis reported (I8), and availability of voxelwise results in the main text (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Decision: EXCLUDE. (a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task is a goal-directed mental rotation requiring spatial transformation operations), I6 (healthy adult group-level whole-brain fMRI effects reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (the manuscript as provided does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space — results are described by Brodmann areas and regions and shown in figures, but no coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates are provided in the full text excerpt). Because all inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I7 is not met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study does not investigate problem solving as defined in the review. The tasks are arbitrary stimulus–response mapping and response-selection paradigms rather than goal-directed problem-solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, or execution to arrive at a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task-based whole-brain fMRI group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the provided definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=28). The task meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations requiring rule-based procedures). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects one-sample t-tests) on data normalized to MNI space and identifies activation clusters (contrast retrieval vs. procedural), and uses BOLD fMRI (EPI) data. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and the paper should be included.

Excluded because the study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The MATRIX task is a visuo-spatial imagery and symmetry-judgment task rather than a problem-solving paradigm involving goal-directed planning/sequencing or execution of operations to discover a previously unknown solution. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain PET group-level analyses in healthy adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports rCBF PET analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED due to failure to satisfy I5.

Although this is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental paradigm does not clearly meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a rule-based letter-matching/branching paradigm focused on working memory and attentional-resource allocation rather than requiring participants to formulate plans or discover solutions to a novel goal-directed problem (i.e., no requirement to generate/sequence actions to reach an unknown solution). The authors discuss links to planning/problem-solving, but the recorded task demands are executive control and rule-following rather than explicit problem solving as defined. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving (a bona fide problem-solving task). It includes longitudinal and cross-sectional whole-brain analyses with group-level effects that include a healthy adult group (n=20) and reports whole-brain contrasts (addition vs control) using stereotactic MNI coordinates for activation peaks. The paper reports BOLD fMRI results and voxelwise analyses (whole-brain and searchlight/multivoxel), with coordinates provided in the main text and figures. It is not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, and includes within-group task effects for healthy adults. The supplied full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=42) using BOLD fMRI during mental arithmetic tasks (multiplication and subtraction), which qualify as problem-solving (goal-directed computation). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and includes voxelwise results presented in tables/figures as well as ROI analyses. All required criteria are met: task-based fMRI of a problem-solving task (I5), whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), coordinates in MNI space (I7), BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and reporting of voxelwise coordinate results in main text/figures (I9). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task is an explicit rule-learning/problem-solving task requiring goal-directed hypothesis generation, evaluation, and application of rule sets (I5). Uses task-based event-related fMRI in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain SPM analyses (I6). Reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7). Reports BOLD (T2*-weighted) analyses (I8). Voxelwise results and coordinates are presented in main text/figures/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only report, no patient-only or between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses BOLD fMRI and reports stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), satisfying I7 and I8 (and I9, since coordinates/voxelwise results are reported). However, it does not meet the key inclusion requirements: (a) the task is a modified PASAT (verbal working memory/attention/arithmetic), which is primarily a working memory/attention task and does not clearly meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met); and (b) the imaging analysis is restricted to predefined ROIs (pre-specified Brodmann-area ROIs) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise analysis, so it reports ROI-only results, triggering exclusion criterion E3 (Reports only region of interest results) and failing I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis). Full text appears complete. Therefore the article must be excluded.

The study uses task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults performing mental calculation (meets I5: problem-solving-like arithmetic task; I6: group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults; I8: BOLD analysis reported). However, the full text as provided does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations nor does it clearly indicate that voxelwise coordinates are available in tables/figures/supplement; therefore I7 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is missing, the study must be excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation including a mental calculation task (silent subtraction), which meets the review definition of a problem-solving task (goal: compute result; requires figuring out procedure). It reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses on 81 healthy adult subjects, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI (3T EPI) with voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. The Penn Conditional Exclusion Test (abstraction/mental flexibility) clearly involves goal-directed rule inference and application consistent with the meta-analysis definition of problem-solving (I5). The paper reports whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in a healthy adult sample (I6) using BOLD fMRI (I8) and describes normalization to standard MNI space; group-level activation maps and a referenced supplementary table summarize task activation (consistent with stereotactic reporting conventions), satisfying I7 and I9. Although ROI extractions are used for prediction, the manuscript also describes whole-brain thresholded group maps (not limited to ROI-only results), so it does not meet exclusion E3. Participants are healthy adults and the full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore include.

This is an event-related, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that uses deductive syllogistic reasoning (logical problem-solving) as the task, matching the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-based logical operations). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholded maps) and explicitly states Talairach-space transformation and localization of significant activations; BOLD contrast analyses are described in methods and results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and indicates voxelwise group results (maps/ROIs/thresholding) that would meet the requirement for stereotactic reporting (figures/tables). Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (N=13) that examines cognitive operations including serial subtraction (rule-based arithmetic) performed to reach task goals (memorize words while performing calculations), which fits the review’s operational definition of problem-solving (goal-directed, rule-based operations). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses, uses Talairach normalization, and presents activation results (Table 2/figures) derived from BOLD signal contrasts between task conditions. Therefore it meets I5 (goal-directed, rule-based arithmetic/dual-task), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While the study uses task-based whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults and reports BOLD results in standard space, its task (causal verbal fluency: generating causes/reasons to cue words) does not meet the review's definition of problem-solving (I5). The CVF paradigm primarily involves semantic retrieval and causal association during word production rather than a goal-directed problem-solving process that requires planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct or novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized stereotactic space/MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a defined problem-solving task per the meta-analysis definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). Although the authors interpret false-statement verification as engaging reasoning/problem-solving processes, the experimental paradigm is a semantic feature-verification/true–false judgment rather than a designed problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or generation of previously unknown solutions. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=19, 18 analyzed) that investigates two-digit mental addition requiring rule-based operations to arrive at correct results, meeting the review definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (using SPM2) with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/TC coordinates) for task-related activations and provides detailed BOLD results and contrasts. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a problem-solving paradigm adapted from Raven’s Progressive Matrices (goal-directed reasoning requiring inference, planning/sequencing and rule-based operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (N=16), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activations, and uses BOLD fMRI contrasts (voxelwise whole-brain results and ROI analyses). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis’ definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment uses a visuospatial judgment (ANGLE vs COLOR) perceptual/categorical decision task (classifying angles or colors) rather than engaging higher-order problem-solving processes involving planning, sequencing, or generating solutions under a rule set to reach a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI RFX analyses), I7 (Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results available) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Exclusion decision: The study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (task is semantic decision/knowledge retrieval about object function/visuospatial properties, not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning, evaluation, sequencing, or execution to find a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, not a patient-group-only or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I5.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in I5. It uses verbal and spatial working memory (item-recognition) tasks (articulatory rehearsal, phonological maintenance, visuospatial maintenance), which do not meet the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed discovery/planning/sequencing to reach previously unknown solutions). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria are triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that used an arithmetic equation-verification task (single-digit addition and multiplication) requiring evaluation and execution of rule-based operations to reach correct judgments. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, describes voxelwise contrasts between tasks and problem sizes, and references activation loci in figures/tables (standard normalization procedures were used). BOLD fMRI results are reported. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for a task-based fMRI study of problem-solving in healthy adults, with whole-brain analyses and reported voxelwise results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD effects; however, the experimental tasks are semantic relation judgments (taxonomic and sequential relation decisions) rather than explicit problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution). Thus it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Included criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in I5. It uses a four-choice visuospatial attention/choice reaction time task focused on attention and movement preparation rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or generating previously unknown solutions. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm per provided definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=10) using mental arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication) that requires goal-directed problem solving under rule-based operations. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected clusters), uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (e.g., hIPS coordinates). Voxelwise results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-only, includes within-group healthy task effects, not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants that requires subjects to infer and apply novel syntactic rules from sample strings (a goal-directed rule-learning task). The task involves identifying and applying a rule to judge strings (inductive rule inference and execution), meeting the review’s definition of problem solving. Group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses are reported, with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results detailed. The full text provides introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task used (same–different memory judgment of symbol strings) did not require subjects to pursue a goal-oriented problem-solving process (planning, sequencing operations, or finding a solution); the authors explicitly state the task did not require explicit syntactic parsing or mathematical calculation. It does meet I6 (group whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results presented). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not patient/group-only, empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because I5 is not satisfied.

This study is an fMRI investigation of moral reasoning using dilemma decision-making in adults including a healthy control group. It meets I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinate results in MNI space via tables/figures), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is moral reasoning/decision-making (evaluating dilemmas and agreeing/disagreeing), not a domain-general problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing operations within rule sets to derive a novel solution). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis because it does not satisfy the essential I5 problem-solving task criterion. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results) — the authors conducted ROI-based analyses and explicitly state a whole-brain approach was not used; E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect) — the analysis uses extant fMRI datasets drawn from participants with Williams syndrome only (no healthy adult group-level task effects are reported for the current analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analyses) — the study uses fMRI BOLD measures. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task; tasks are passive listening/viewing with low cognitive load), I6 (does not include whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results for whole-brain task effects in healthy adults), I9 (no voxelwise whole-brain results reported for healthy adults). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study of propositional analogical reasoning (a fluid reasoning/problem-solving task) that includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript presents voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and multiple regression results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., left RLPFC at −27, 50, 0; right RLPFC at 27, 45, 16), and uses BOLD fMRI. Results are reported across whole-brain maps and ROI follow-ups; they are not limited to ROI-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants examining deductive (syllogistic) reasoning, which constitutes problem-solving via logical operations (meets I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM (MNI normalization) in healthy adults (meets I6). Results are reported as BOLD fMRI effects with stereotactic coordinates/peak locations (MNI/Talairach) and tables/figures (meets I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not investigate problem-solving as defined (I5). It is a task-based fMRI study of semantic property-verification (perceptual knowledge) rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing or critical thinking to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This PET study uses healthy adult subjects and reports whole-brain group analysis of rCBF (meets I6 and I8). However, the task is the Hayling Test probing verbal initiation and suppression (response initiation/inhibition and word retrieval), which does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a solution (I5 not met). In the provided full text there are descriptions of regional activations but stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not present in the text supplied, so I7 cannot be confirmed (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I7.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using a syllogistic deductive-reasoning task. The reasoning task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (participants have the goal of deciding whether a conclusion follows and must determine how to reach that decision). The study reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPM8), reports stereotactic MNI coordinates in the text and supplementary tables/figures, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. Voxelwise results are reported in supplementary tables and main text figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n≈15 in imaging analyses) using a reasoning task (syllogistic inference) where participants had the explicit goal to judge whether a conclusion follows from premises (i.e., goal-directed computation fitting the provided problem-solving definition). Group-level, whole-brain analyses are reported with stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations and interaction contrasts. BOLD (fMRI) analyses are used and voxelwise results are reported in the main text and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, participants are healthy adults, task effects within the healthy group are reported, and the paper is empirical with original data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD effects and group-level analyses, the task (mental clock imagery and angle comparison) is a visuospatial imagery/angle-comparison task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed multi-step problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule sets). The full text shows whole-brain group analyses (n=6), BOLD methods, and figures of statistical maps, but stereotactic coordinate tables are not provided in the supplied text (so I7 is not clearly satisfied). Therefore I6, I8, and I9 are met but I5 (problem-solving task) and I7 (reported stereotactic coordinates) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI investigation reporting voxelwise BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates in a sample that includes healthy adult controls. It therefore meets I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the experimental paradigm is a verbal working-memory (delayed match-to-sample with manipulation) / executive task rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). The task mainly probes working memory/manipulation and does not clearly operationalize problem solving per the meta-analysis definition. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I5.

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (I5). The task consists of reading stories about mental versus physical states and rating likelihood/surprise; it assesses theory of mind and attention to unexpected stimuli rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing, or executing operations to reach a solution. The paper does meet other methodological criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level random effects analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results in the main text/analyses (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that explicitly examines problem solving (insight into real-world technical problems using heuristic prototypes). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (RP > UP), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This PET study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The task is simultaneous language interpreting/translation, which involves language comprehension, lexical search, and working memory rather than goal-directed problem solving/planning/sequencing to derive a novel solution. The study does meet several methodological inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level PET analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports rCBF PET task-related analyses (I8), and the main text indicates voxelwise results are available (I9). However, stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI space are not explicitly provided in the supplied full text excerpt (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper should be excluded because it fails to meet I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm) and I7 (coordinates not clearly reported in the provided text).

Although this is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults examining cognitive set-shifting on the Trail Making Test (meeting I5, I6, and I8), the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) or tables of voxelwise coordinates for task-related increases. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinate results) is not satisfied in the supplied content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete for core sections, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses the Tower of London (ToL) planning task, which qualifies as a problem-solving paradigm (I5), and it reports stereotactic coordinates (I7) from BOLD fMRI analyses (I8) with coordinates available in the text (I9). However, it does not present a whole-brain, group-level task activation map for healthy adults relevant to problem-solving. The reported imaging results focus on genotype-related correlations and diagnosis-by-genotype interactions (including ROI-based PFC findings) rather than reporting whole-brain task-related group effects in the healthy control group. The authors report that no other areas emerged as significant in whole-brain analyses for the ToL, and the principal ToL effects appear to be reported within an ROI framework. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (doesn't include healthy-group task effects/only between-group/genotype contrasts relevant to this review). Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level BOLD study in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise results (Table 3, figures). However, the experimental task is a visuospatial discrimination/perception task (selecting a target figure) rather than a problem-solving task as defined for the meta-analysis (goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing, executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Exclusion rationale: The study investigates visuospatial working memory in a clinical sample (ARMS) and healthy controls using task-based fMRI, but the task is not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing/critical evaluation to arrive at a novel solution). This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task).

The fMRI in this study used a three-back working memory task with lure and non-lure trials to probe attentional control and its relation to fluid intelligence. While the paper assesses Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving measure) outside the scanner, the neuroimaging task itself is a working-memory/interference-control task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The study meets inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/tabled). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5 (imaging task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition).

Excluded because the task is a phonological verbal fluency (generate words beginning with a letter), which is primarily lexical retrieval/fluency and does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5) requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing, and execution to arrive at a (previously unknown) solution. The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level PET analyses including healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports rCBF/PET analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/coordinated results reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a Chinese-character chunk-decomposition problem-solving task that requires goal-directed representational change and execution of operations to generate valid characters (meets I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses (2×2 factorial), with stereotactic coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and cluster results presented (meets I6 and I7). BOLD fMRI analyses are reported and thresholding/cluster inference are described (meets I8). Voxelwise results appear in tables/figures and are clearly available (meets I9). Participants were healthy adult students (N=16, 14 analyzed). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not clinical group comparisons only, include healthy-group task effects, and this is empirical primary research. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the above, the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of problem-solving (word vs number problems) in healthy adults. It uses group-level whole-brain analyses (ANOVA and contrasts versus fixation), reports BOLD/fMRI results, and data were normalized to MNI space with activation maps and contrasts described (coordinates/voxelwise results indicated to be in figures/tables). The participant sample are healthy young adults (n=15 analyzed). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, clinical/group-comparison-only, non-empirical) are met.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. This fMRI study investigates semantic list learning and long-term memory encoding (Papez circuit) using a Brown–Peterson manipulation. It is not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed need to figure out novel solutions, planning/sequencing to reach a solution, or critical-thinking operations to derive a correct/novel answer). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (compound remote associate problems) in healthy adults, using whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis reporting BOLD results. The paper reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., peak at 44, -9, -9) and describes whole-brain cluster-thresholding procedures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using Raven’s Standard Progressive Matrices (a clear problem‑solving/fluid reasoning task). Note: sample age range includes 14–36, but analyses include healthy non‑autistic adults. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study meets multiple methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group fMRI in healthy adults with reported stereotactic results and BOLD analyses), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in I5. The task involves perceptual ratings and belief-revision/evidence-integration (rating two morphed animal images and updating belief), which constitutes perceptual decision-making and evidence evaluation rather than a goal-directed problem-solving process requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct or novel solution. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This study uses task-based fMRI (BOLD) in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain analyses, but the cognitive tasks (visual angle/color discrimination and a mental-clock visuospatial imagery comparison) do not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Additionally, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI peak coordinates for task-related increases (I7) in the excerpt supplied. The paper does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis) and I8 (BOLD analysis). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5 (and lacking explicit coordinate reporting I7/I9 in the provided text).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain analyses, but it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The experimental tasks are semantic synonymy/relatedness judgments about object manipulation vs. function (deciding whether object pairs share a function or are manipulated similarly), which are semantic decision tasks rather than goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning, sequencing, or executing operations to arrive at an unknown solution (I5 not met). While the study includes whole-brain group analyses (I6) and reports BOLD results (I8), the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinate peaks in the excerpt (I7 not demonstrably met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided information. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5 (and, based on the provided text, I7).

This is a task-based fMRI study in 16 healthy adults performing an arithmetic (serial addition) task that requires goal-directed operations and rule-based computation, which fits the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study used whole-brain acquisition and performed group-level mixed-effects analyses (I6), reported BOLD fMRI results (I8), and normalized data to the MNI template with voxelwise results reported in the contrasts and figures/tables (I7, I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core content appears present.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult novice participants performing a multiple-choice electric-circuit task that requires judging correctness (a goal-directed problem-solving/decision task). The study reports whole-brain group-level SPM analyses on BOLD data, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates and tables/figures of task-related activations, and voxelwise results are reported. All inclusion criteria (I5–I9) are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (it includes group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is a similarity-judgment/working-memory labeling task, not a problem-solving task as defined by a goal plus needing to figure out a way to reach it) and I7 (the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space for task-related activations in the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adult participants (n=20) involving a goal-directed strategic game (Beauty Contest) in which subjects must select numbers to win—requiring evaluation, planning/predictive reasoning about others, and execution of operations conforming to game rules (meets I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (I6), provides task-related activation coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the text/supplementary (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not limited to ROIs only and the paper is empirical with healthy-group task effects. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). It reports an fMRI experiment of visuo-motor synchronization and verbal rehearsal to parse sequential brain activations, not a goal-directed problem solving task involving planning/evaluating to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (data normalized to standard space and coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results described and coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria applied (E3–E6 not met). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED for failing I5.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using Raven's Progressive Matrices—an established problem-solving/fluid-reasoning task—conducted in healthy adults (n=79). Whole-brain analyses were performed (group-level ICA, within-subject ANOVA on spatial maps and FNC analyses). The paper uses BOLD fMRI data and reports spatial results in standard MNI space (figures reference MNI152 standard space and Supplementary Table I contains voxel locations), satisfying coordinate reporting. Voxelwise results are available in figures/supplement. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

The study is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults with group-level random effects analyses and reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results. However, it does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined (a task that first has a goal and then requires figuring out a way to reach it). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related, task-based BOLD fMRI study in 16 healthy adult participants that directly examines logical problem-solving (inductive and deductive reasoning) — a task involving goal-directed inference and application of rule-based operations (meets I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses using SPM with spatial normalization to an MNI template and statistical parametric maps (meets I6 and I7). BOLD analyses are reported (meets I8). Although coordinate tables/figures are referenced but not shown in the excerpt, the article indicates stereotactic reporting consistent with standard fMRI practice and allows coordinates in tables/figures (meets I9). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study using a verification/arithmetical reasoning task in healthy adult participants (N=16). The arithmetic verification requires goal-directed evaluation and execution of rule-based operations (compute and compare answers), which falls within the review’s problem-solving definition (evaluation and execution within an algebraic rule set). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM) in healthy adults, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic (Talairach) localization with tables/figures of activation foci. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults using a well-defined problem-solving task (trial-and-error search to discover a correct stimulus, requiring evaluation, planning/selection, and execution), satisfying I5. It reports group-level whole-brain analyses (mixed-effects random effects, cluster-corrected) and results (coordinates reported in MNI space), satisfying I6 and I7. It reports BOLD analyses (fMRI BOLD signal, percent signal change, RPE modulation), satisfying I8. Coordinate results and voxelwise findings are presented in the main text and supplemental materials, satisfying I9. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment of verbal problem solving (compound remote associates) in healthy adult participants, using whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses of BOLD signal. The manuscript describes event-related contrasts of preparation intervals for insight vs. noninsight trials, reports cluster-based voxelwise results and refers to Tabulated stereotactic coordinates (Table 1) and figures. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based problem-solving paradigm), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study used an fMRI verbal working memory (Sternberg-style) task in hemodialysis patients and matched controls, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations to derive a novel solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The paper does include whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses and reports stereotactic MNI coordinates, and includes healthy adult controls, but the primary reported effects concern group-by-time interactions related to dialysis; the manuscript does not present a clear task-related whole-brain activation effect for healthy controls alone (no main-effect task activation in controls reported). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts or no healthy-group task effect) applies. Summary: meets I6, I7, I8, I9; does not meet I5; exclusion E5 applies, so the study is excluded.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of integral-calculus problem solving in healthy adult participants, using a goal-directed integration verification task that requires rule-based operations and evaluation. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise BOLD results (q(FDR)<.05) and provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates (Table 1). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=28) that investigates problem-solving across two domains (complex multiplication and figural-spatial problems). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (voxelwise FWE-corrected results) and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space in tables. The imaging measure is BOLD fMRI (EPI sequence), and multiple whole-brain contrasts (trained vs. untrained; task contrasts) are presented with cluster coordinates. The tasks qualify as problem-solving (goal-directed computation or spatial reasoning to derive previously unknown solutions). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/age/gender-only comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is provided and appears complete.

The study employed a task (anomalous categorisation with requirement to generate alternative categories and avoid repeats) that entails goal-directed strategy use, self-ordered selection and planning to achieve the task goal, consistent with a problem-solving definition involving strategy generation and selection. It reports a task-based fMRI BOLD study in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain analyses (group GBAMs), spatial normalisation to Talairach space with reported stereotactic coordinates (example coordinate provided), and voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Note small sample (n=6 in group analysis) but group-level whole-brain effects are reported.

Although this is an empirical fMRI BOLD study with healthy adult participants, whole-brain group analyses, and stereotactic coordinates reported, the task is a creative literary text-continuation task rather than a defined problem-solving task per the review's I5 definition. The task lacks an explicit goal-to-solution structure with objectively correct or rule-governed solutions; it emphasizes originality/appropriateness and qualitative creativity ratings rather than planning/executing operations to reach a defined solution. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met despite meeting other imaging criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is sentence-creation to form semantic associations for memory encoding, not a goal-directed problem-solving operation involving planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct solution. It does, however, meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level, whole-brain fMRI analyses), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). No exclusion criteria are met (exclusion IDs: none). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Therefore EXCLUDED.

Full text is complete. This fMRI study (n=14 healthy adults) investigates response shifting / task switching (executive control, attention) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-setting plus planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the experimental task is response shifting/task-switching, not a problem-solving paradigm involving goal-directed planning or novel solution generation). This task-based fMRI study examines an executive verbal working memory task in healthy adults that requires goal-directed, rule-based manipulation (counting two letters forward and evaluating membership), which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem-solving (operations conforming to a rule set to arrive at a correct solution). The study uses whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in 16 healthy adults, reports BOLD fMRI results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI, with Talairach transformation), and provides voxelwise coordinate results in the main text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included in the review.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of verbal working memory (Sternberg variant) in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with MNI coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is a working memory manipulation (count two letters forward and rehearse) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions to reach a novel solution). The paradigm tests inner speech and maintenance/manipulation processes, not cross-domain problem solving. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failing I5.

The task (reverse recitation of months) requires rule-based sequencing and manipulation of verbal items, consistent with the review’s definition of problem-solving (planning/sequencing operations to achieve a goal). The study used task-based whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults (n=18) with voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses reporting Talairach coordinates and BOLD signal changes. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of deductive (syllogistic) reasoning in 14 healthy adults. The task entails deriving logical conclusions from premises (goal-directed, rule-based operations consistent with the review's problem-solving definition). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM with activations reported as stereotactic coordinates (normalized to the MNI template) and BOLD contrast results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-only, not non-empirical). Thus all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied.

Excluded because the experimental task is a visuo-spatial recognition/memory task with feedback and rewards, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to discover a previously unknown solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported via Talairach/SPM mapping), I8 (rCBF PET analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in standard space). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the review definition). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This study investigates cognitive empathy and mentalizing using false-belief cartoon stories, not problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition). I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting) is not evident in the provided full text excerpt. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not address problem-solving tasks as required by I5.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=25) using a multiplication verification task that requires goal-directed, rule-based operations (identifying correctness of arithmetic solutions), satisfying the definition of problem solving. The authors performed whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and regression) and report stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (e.g., peak x = -50, y = -64, z = 28). BOLD contrast results and voxelwise cluster statistics are presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, clinical/age/gender-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the task does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment investigates hierarchical visuo-spatial sequence processing and grammaticality judgments of learned artificial grammar rules rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution or applying critical-thinking processes to solve a presented problem. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of conditional/logical reasoning (Wason card selection), which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving (evaluating rules and executing logical operations). It reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise thresholds reported) in healthy adult participants (N=16). Results include stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and BOLD fMRI analyses. Although ROI analyses are also reported, whole-brain voxelwise results are presented. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing single-digit multiplication problems (a problem-solving task). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, including contrasts of interest (large vs. small problems) and inter-group comparisons. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and derive from BOLD fMRI analyses; voxelwise cluster results are presented (tables/figures). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication) including healthy adult participants and whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (arithmetic tasks are rule-based problem-solving operations), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI). I9 is likely satisfied insofar as voxelwise results and activation maps are described. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the material given here, and I7 therefore cannot be confirmed. Note: figures/tables and coordinate listings appear to be omitted from the supplied text (placeholders present), but the core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present; fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20) that used an inductive logical reasoning task (syllogisms) requiring subjects to evaluate premises and derive conclusions, which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed reasoning within a logical rule set). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9 and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used mental arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication) as goal-directed, rule-based problem-solving tasks, satisfying I5. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in 18 healthy adults (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and normalization to MNI space with reported activation peaks (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only analyses, no patient/group-only contrasts, empirical healthy-subject task effects present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of an arithmetic problem-solving task in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain analyses and BOLD contrasts reported, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic peak coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the main text. While ROI center coordinates (from a meta-analysis) and references to Figures/Tables are present, explicit voxelwise peak coordinates for the reported activations are not shown in the provided material. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this is a whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses a Kanji-grapheme puzzle (a goal-directed puzzle requiring combination of parts) and reports BOLD activation and group-level effects, the full text provided does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or indicate that voxelwise coordinate tables/figures/supplementary materials with coordinates are available. Inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis), and I8 (BOLD analysis) are met. Inclusion criterion I7 (reports task-related increases as stereotactic coordinate results) is not met based on the provided full text, and I9 (presence of coordinates in tables/figures/supplement) is not verifiable from the text. Therefore the study cannot be included. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used an N-Back working memory task (a continuous performance/working memory paradigm), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring figuring out a way to reach a goal). Although it is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study with group analyses, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations in the excerpt, and the task domain does not match the meta-analysis target (problem solving). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning in healthy adult participants (n=14 analyzed) that examines complex reasoning/problem-solving processes (evaluating and integrating relations to judge analogies). It includes whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses using BOLD fMRI, reports stereotactic (Talairach/ROI) coordinates and voxelwise results, and presents task-related activation contrasts. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis definitions of a problem-solving task (semantic/relational reasoning) and meets inclusion criteria I5–I9. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, and is empirical with original human data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (n=20) using the PASAT/PVSAT. The task requires repeated arithmetic operations (apply a rule to add the current and previous digit) and thus involves rule-based operations and execution to arrive at correct responses, satisfying the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for activations/deactivations, and presents task-related BOLD results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and no exclusion criteria apply. Note: PASAT is primarily a working-memory/arithmetic task and borderline with respect to higher-order problem solving, but it fits the review’s definition of rule-based operations to arrive at correct solutions and so is included.

This is an empirical whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a mental-arithmetic paradigm that requires goal-directed problem solving (integration/segregation of maintained digits into multi-step arithmetic)—meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space in tables (I7, I9), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, patient-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it should be included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a mental-rotation task that requires goal-directed spatial transformation and rule-based discrimination (same/different), which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (Compare vs Control), presents voxelwise activation maps and tables, and uses Talairach coordinates (I6,I7). BOLD signal (fMRI) results are reported with percent signal change and regressions relating behavior to activation (I8). Voxelwise results are available in figures/tables (I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, not a non-empirical paper, includes within-group task effects).

This study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The experiments are categorical and coordinate spatial judgment tasks (perceptual/decision tasks) rather than problem-solving paradigms that require setting a goal and devising a means/strategy to reach it. It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses reported), I7 (results/methods report MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI reported), and I9 (voxelwise/ROI and whole-brain results are described and available). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3, E4, E5, E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails the essential inclusion criterion I5.

This is an event-related whole-brain fMRI study in 19 healthy adult subjects that uses logical reasoning (syllogism) tasks. The tasks constitute problem solving under the review definition (goal-directed logical operations within a rule set). The paper reports group-level whole-brain SPM analyses with stereotactic coordinates referenced to the MNI template and BOLD contrast results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study uses a 2-Back working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). It meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, BOLD analyses, and acceptable voxelwise reporting), but it does not investigate problem-solving processes (planning/sequencing to arrive at unknown solutions) required by I5. The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This is a task-based PET study of problem solving (Tower of Toronto/Hanoi), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=12). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM99, provides rCBF (H2O15 PET) task-related activation results, and presents stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables and figures). The study thus satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (rCBF analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE for the review.

This is an empirical, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, voxelwise results in MNI space following task manipulation (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is complex visuomotor skill training (Space Fortress ship-control) focused on motor control, visuospatial attention, and skill acquisition rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed critical thinking/planning to derive novel or rule-based solutions). Therefore I5 (study of a problem-solving task per the review definition) is not met. No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are triggered). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks are perceptual/spatial judgment and mental transformation (left-right judgments, mental rotation/perspective taking) rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a novel solution. It does, however, report group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults using BOLD (I6, I8) and presents voxelwise activation maps/standardized-space analyses in figures (I9). It is unclear from the provided text whether stereotactic peak coordinates (Talairach/MNI) are reported in tables or text, so I7 is not satisfied based on the excerpt. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because inclusion criterion I5 is not met (and I7 not clearly met).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that includes mental arithmetic and calendrical calculation tasks (both fitting the review's problem-solving definition) and reports BOLD (fMRI) results as stereotactic coordinates. However, it does not provide group-level whole-brain effects in healthy adults: participants comprise two autistic calendrical savants (single-case analyses) and a single healthy control participant. Analyses are case-study/conjunction and region-guided single-subject contrasts rather than group-level healthy adult whole-brain statistics. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (no healthy-group task effect/group-level healthy adult results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults performing mental calculation tasks that constitute problem-solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations requiring sequencing and rule-based execution). It used whole-brain EPI coverage and group-level random-effects analyses, reported BOLD contrasts (complex vs simple) with voxelwise results and stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach). Voxelwise results, conjunction analyses, thresholds, and anatomical localization are provided in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison-only, and not non-empirical). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental subtraction in healthy adults and therefore examines a calculation procedure (I5). It includes group-level whole-brain EPI analyses in healthy adult participants (I6) and uses T2*-weighted BOLD imaging (I8). However, the paper does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (no x,y,z coordinate tables or coordinate-labeled figures are provided); results are described by Brodmann areas and region labels only. Because it fails to meet I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting), it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an empirical whole-brain BOLD fMRI investigation with healthy adult controls, reports stereotactic coordinates, and provides group-level analyses; however, it does NOT examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (it investigates Theory of Mind/mentalizing using animated shapes, not goal-directed problem solving, planning, or execution within a rule-based framework). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis imaging requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the PET analysis is reported using striatal ROIs/[11C]raclopride binding measures rather than whole-brain, voxelwise, task-related analyses). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (requires a task-based fMRI or PET study of problem-solving; here cognitive problem-solving (Tower of London) was behavioral but PET was not task-based), I6 (no whole-brain group-level task activation analysis reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported for task-related activations), I8 (no BOLD or task-related rCBF analysis reported), I9 (no voxelwise task results provided in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis as it lacks task-based whole-brain neuroimaging results required by the review.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants that explicitly uses a reasoning/problem-solving task requiring deduction and application of a sequence rule (goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-based solution), satisfying the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (FDR-corrected maps), normalization to MNI space, and refers to stereotactic coordinates; it includes voxelwise results and an fMRI BOLD analysis. ROI analyses are present but do not replace whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Supplementary/Data statements, so fulltext appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning (conditional and syllogistic problems), which qualifies as problem-solving: participants had goals (derive valid conclusions) and engaged critical-thinking processes (encoding, integration, rule-based/logical operations) to produce previously unknown conclusions. Methods: 26 healthy adult participants, whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level random-effects analyses, normalized to MNI space, and voxelwise results reported (tables/figures and supplementary unthresholded maps). The paper reports task-related BOLD increases and stereotactic coordinates (MNI). Design and analyses satisfy whole-brain group inference requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.
