This paper reports an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using a mental rotation task that requires goal-directed mental transformation operations to determine object congruency. The study used whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with SPM2, reports region-level activation results and (per main text and supplementary mention) stereotactic localization, and measures BOLD responses. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements: task-based neuroimaging of a goal-directed cognitive operation (mental rotation), whole-brain group effects, stereotactic reporting, and BOLD analyses. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplementary data referenced. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study includes a task that meets the review definition of problem-solving (Tower of London visuospatial planning) and reports task-based fMRI BOLD analyses (I5 and I8). However, all reported functional results are constrained to predefined ROIs and corrected with small-volume correction; no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task effects in healthy adults are reported in the main text (results are ROI-based). Thus the study reports only ROI results and does not provide the required whole-brain group-level healthy-task activations (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults) and I7 (stereotactic coordinate results for whole-brain task effects) are not satisfied based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines mental transformations of melodies. The tasks require goal-directed mental operations (judging whether a second melody is a transposition or reversal of the first), involving evaluation, sequencing/planning of mental operations, and execution of rule-based transformations—meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses using standardized MNI space coordinates, and BOLD-based results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of arithmetic calculation in healthy adults and aphasic patients. It meets I5 (arithmetic calculation fits the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task), I6 (includes a healthy adult control group with second-level whole-brain analysis), and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). However, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the excerpt supplied, and I7 is therefore not satisfied based on the available content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so this exclusion is due to missing explicit stereotactic coordinate reporting in the provided text, not due to incomplete article content.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a social decision-making/Ultimatum Game probing fairness and intentionality, not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a previously unknown solution. While the paper reports whole-brain stereotactic (MNI) BOLD results (meets I7 and I8) and provides coordinate data (I9), it does not provide whole-brain group-level analyses specifically targeting a healthy adult problem-solving task (I6 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of a mathematical problem-solving task in healthy participants and includes whole-brain analyses and BOLD-based results, but the provided full text does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the excerpt supplied. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based problem-solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD analysis). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I7 (no explicit stereotactic coordinate results reported in the provided text). I9 (acceptable reporting in figures/tables) may be implied by references to figures, but explicit coordinates in standardized space are not present in the provided content. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study uses a non-verbal WCST-like paradigm that requires subjects to derive sorting rules by trial-and-error, detect rule changes, engage in inductive reasoning, feedback integration, and rule generation—processes that meet the review's operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule discovery and execution). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (14 male volunteers), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) with tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s problem-solving task definition (I5). The task is a visuospatial discrimination/perceptual-speed task (same/different color placement) rather than a problem-solving paradigm requiring planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. The provided full text does include whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6, I8) and indicates voxelwise results/figures are available (I9). However, the manuscript as provided does not include explicit stereotactic coordinate tables or reported Talairach/MNI coordinates in the text supplied (I7 not met in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore EXCLUDED. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I7. Exclusion IDs met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that examines goal-directed behavior (delivering customers to destinations) requiring route choice, planning/sequencing of actions, and compliance with traffic rules. These components map onto the review's problem-solving definition (I5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with full-brain coverage (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Coordinate results and peak activations are reported in tables/figures (I9). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of problem-solving tasks across domains.

While this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD analyses, the experimental paradigm investigates verbal humor comprehension (incongruity detection and resolution) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined in the review (i.e., having an explicit goal and requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to reach a solution within a rule framework). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. It does meet I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: it does not report at least one whole‑brain, group‑level analysis limited to healthy adult participants. Although an adult subgroup (22.5–30.4 years) is included, the reported whole‑brain Relational>Control results are presented averaged across all age groups, and the effective‑connectivity (DCM) analyses are ROI‑based rather than whole‑brain voxelwise results for the adult group alone. The paper does meet I5 (relational reasoning task qualifies as problem‑solving), I7 (results reported in MNI space/with stereotactic references), I8 (BOLD fMRI reported), and I9 (voxelwise results/tables available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided full text.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI study of a problem-solving task (anagram solving) in healthy adults; reports group-level whole-brain analyses using BOLD fMRI; results are reported in standardized stereotactic (MNI) space with coordinate tables/figures; voxelwise/task-related increases are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full article text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of methods and stereotactic results. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET problem-solving in healthy adults.

Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standard space), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task is moral decision-making between personal desire and moral standard, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review which requires goal-directed problem solving with planning/sequencing and execution within a rule-based framework). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task per the I5 definition.

The study uses a Tower of London task (problem-solving) and BOLD fMRI (I5 and I8 satisfied). However, the imaging analysis is ROI/VOI-based on individually delineated anatomy without normalization to a standard stereotactic space and without reporting stereotactic coordinates (no Talairach/MNI coordinates). There is no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis reported for healthy adults. Therefore it fails to meet I6 (no whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults) and I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results). This study effectively reports only ROI results (E3). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study includes a visuospatial planning (Tower of London) task that meets the definition of problem-solving/planning (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level imaging analyses (SPM whole-brain t tests) and includes a healthy adult control group used in post hoc group comparisons (I6). Task-related BOLD fMRI results are reported, and main task effects and coordinates are stated as available in Supplementary Table S7 (satisfying I7 and I8); reporting of voxelwise results in supplementary materials satisfies I9. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion; supplementary coordinate tables are indicated. No exclusion criteria are met. Consequently the study qualifies for inclusion in the review of whole-brain, task-based fMRI studies of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (BOLD) in healthy adult participants (n=21) that directly examines problem-solving processes: dominance-solvable games require stepwise deliberative reasoning (goal identification, planning/iterated elimination of strategies, and rule-based execution), and coordination games engage intuitive salience judgments. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts with frontoparietal, insula, and ACC activations and refers to stereotactic coordinate tables in the supplementary material (tables S2, S3, etc.), indicating voxelwise results are available. Thus it meets I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results in tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary tables are referenced and their absence here is acceptable.

This is a task-based fMRI (BOLD) study in healthy adults using a rule-based conditional reasoning/problem-solving task (Wason selection-style rule-broken task) that requires identifying violations and applying logical/deontic rules to arrive at correct responses, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The study performed whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses on 24 healthy adults with images normalized to MNI space and reported region/cluster activations (I6, I8). The Methods state normalization to the MNI template and report stereotactic activations (BAs/clusters) with statistical thresholds and figures/tables implied, satisfying reporting of stereotactic results (I7) and allowing voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to group-difference-only contrasts (E5), not non-empirical (E6), nor solely disease/age/gender comparisons (E4). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=16 analyzed) that examines cognitive processes involved in single-digit multiplication (goal-directed computation, rule application, strategy use), which qualifies as problem solving per the review definition. The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM2 with normalization to MNI space and reports task-related BOLD effects (contrasts: small/large/zero multiplications vs. storage and between-condition contrasts). Voxelwise results and anatomical labels are presented; supplementary coordinate data are indicated as available. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study investigates Theory of Mind / social cognition using a naturalistic video-based task (MASC). It is not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem-solving, planning/sequencing or rule-based solution operations), so it fails inclusion criterion I5. The study does include whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6) and reports BOLD-based analyses (I8). However, it does not report stereotactic coordinates in the provided full text (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving as required by the review (I5 not met).

The study uses a visuo-spatial mental rotation / mirror-image judgement task, which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) that requires goal-directed planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations to arrive at a solution. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and reports BOLD fMRI results (I8); voxelwise results are reported in the main text/figures (I9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a PET (rCBF) whole-brain, task-based imaging study in healthy adult groups (young and senior) that reports group-level voxelwise contrasts with stereotactic coordinates and Brodmann-area localization. The Operation Span task includes arithmetic equation evaluation (rule-based algebraic/arithmetic operations) combined with sequential updating and planning-like WM operations, which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed execution of operations conforming to a rule set). The paper provides whole-brain analyses, tables/figures of coordinates, and rCBF PET results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based PET study of logical (deductive) and probabilistic reasoning in healthy adults that meets all inclusion criteria. The tasks constitute problem-solving (deduction/probabilistic judgment over identical propositional stimuli with goal-directed evaluation using formal logical rules), PET rCBF whole-brain analyses are reported with group-level contrasts across 10 healthy adults, stereotactic Talairach coordinates are provided for activation peaks, and voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only or non-empirical paper). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (meets I6) and reports BOLD analyses (meets I8). However, the task is verbal fluency (letter/category word generation), which is a lexical retrieval/executive control task and does not match the meta-analysis definition of problem solving requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct or novel solution (I5 not met). The provided full text also does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates in the excerpt (I7 not met; I9 therefore not applicable). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined and lacks reported stereotactic coordinates in the provided text.

Excluded (E3): The study reports PET results using predefined ROI analyses (regional binding potentials) rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis. Inclusion met: I5 — it is a task-based PET study using an attentive calculation task (problem-focused calculation) in healthy adults. Inclusion NOT met: I6 — no whole-brain voxelwise/group-level whole-brain analysis is reported; I7 — no stereotactic (Talairach/MNI) coordinate results are provided; I8 — the outcomes are PET receptor binding potentials (BP) for H1 receptors, not task-related BOLD or rCBF measures. Full text appears complete. Based on these, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical PET study in healthy adults with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reporting Talairach coordinates and rCBF results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), the tasks investigated (mental rotation, mirror-image discrimination, form/orientation/gap detection) are perceptual/cognitive/tactile discrimination tasks rather than problem-solving tasks as defined in I5 (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution). Therefore I5 is not met, so the study is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) The task is a relational reasoning/problem-solving paradigm requiring participants to infer rules (which dimension changes) and apply logical comparisons to reach correct responses, fitting the meta-analysis definition of problem solving; (I6) Whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses were performed (second-level 2×3 analysis with random effects) that include a healthy adult group; (I7) Stereotactic peak coordinates are reported (e.g. [−48 45 −3], [3 27 42]); (I8) BOLD fMRI analyses are reported; (I9) Voxelwise results and tables/figures are presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes healthy adult task effects; empirical original data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) and F-DOPA PET during an overt verbal fluency task that uses an explicit rule (generate words starting with a letter), which fits the review's definition of problem-solving involving goal-directed, rule-based operations. It includes voxelwise group-level fMRI effects with healthy adult controls (post hoc confirmation of task-related activation in controls), reports stereotactic coordinates (Table 1, figures) in MNI space, and presents whole-brain/task-related BOLD analyses (with reported subcortical activations) and coordinate tables. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study meets the meta-analysis requirements. It reports a task-based whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (n=19) using rCBF PET (H2^15O) and SPM99 normalization to MNI space with stereotactic peak coordinates reported. The semantic decision task requires subjects to evaluate semantic relations among word triplets and select the best-matching item (a goal-directed evaluation of alternatives), which qualifies as a problem-solving-type task under the review definition (evaluation of the problem and execution of rule-based operations to arrive at a correct response). All core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text, and voxelwise coordinate results are reported. Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20) performing numerical inductive reasoning (rule identification and rule application). The tasks require establishing a goal (determine the rule and/or compute the next number) and executing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution, meeting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests) after normalization to an MNI template and provides stereotactic coordinates (e.g., −24 −63 45), and uses BOLD fMRI measures. Results are presented across introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group clinical comparison, and it is empirical). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment using the Wason selection task (logical/conditional reasoning), which qualifies as a problem-solving task involving goal-directed inferential operations and rule-based evaluation. The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (N=12 analyzed), uses BOLD fMRI, and presents stereotactic coordinate results in standard space (MNI) with voxelwise contrasts and cluster thresholds. Voxelwise activation tables/figures and coordinate-based results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, not non-empirical). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling verification of inclusion criteria.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, it does not meet the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment investigates category-based induction and the inclusion fallacy — a comparative semantic/reasoning judgment about which of two inductive arguments is stronger — rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm that requires establishing a goal and figuring out means to achieve it (e.g., planning, multi-step solution search). Therefore I5 is not satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=18) performing arithmetic operations (addition/subtraction) requiring goal-directed calculation and execution, which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, uses an MNI template and provides stereotactic coordinates and t-values in tables/figures, and reports voxelwise BOLD results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a patient-group comparison, not non-empirical, and includes within-healthy-group task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The experiment investigates theory-of-mind (social cognition) — predicting an agent's action from beliefs/desires — rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., having a goal that requires planning/sequencing and executing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution). Although the task involves reasoning and occasional abductive inference (D±), many trials require subjective judgments (D±) and the primary aim is social inference, not domain-general problem solving. The full text is complete and the study does meet I6, I7, I8, and I9 (whole-brain fMRI group analysis in healthy adults; MNI coordinates; BOLD analysis; voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment uses a theory-of-mind/false-vs-true-belief cartoon task requiring mental-state attribution (decoupling belief from reality) and a judgment of expected vs. unexpected outcomes, but it does not involve goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level random-effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5. The task is a mental rotation / visuospatial discrimination task (deciding whether two 3D shapes are identical or mirror images). Although it involves mental transformation of images, it does not meet the review's operational definition of problem-solving (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, execution within a rule-based framework to arrive at a novel or appropriate solution). The study focuses on perceptual/spatial transformation and sex differences in activation rather than problem-solving processes. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of deductive (logical/transitive) problem-solving using acoustically presented transitive-inference problems, which fit the definition of problem solving (goal-directed inference, planning/integration to reach a conclusion). It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (12 right-handed male adults) using BOLD fMRI, and describes voxelwise cluster results and anatomical localization (Brodmann areas) with methods performed in SPM5, indicating stereotactic coordinate results are available in the paper (standardized reporting typical for SPM studies). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task type (I5), group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7), BOLD analysis (I8), and allowance for voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly probes generation of deductive conclusions (modus ponens and disjunction elimination). The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition: participants have the goal of deriving a conclusion and must perform rule-based logical operations to reach a correct solution. The study used whole-brain random-effects analyses in a sample of healthy adults, acquired BOLD fMRI data, normalized images to MNI space, and reports voxelwise activation results with supplementary materials indicated. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic normalization to MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available/supplementary). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text is complete and the study is an fMRI task in healthy adults reporting whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates. It therefore meets criteria I6 (whole-brain group fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise coordinate results reported in tables/figures). However, the experimental paradigm is verbal fluency and task-switching between categories, which is an executive/attentional control task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a correct or novel solution). The manuscript does not describe tasks involving evaluation, planning or sequencing to arrive at a correct/previously unknown solution in the sense required by I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore exclude for not meeting I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study of logical/deductive reasoning (meets I5) and uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8). However, the paper does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations (fails I7) and does not present voxelwise, whole-brain group-level coordinate results for healthy adults; group comparisons are based on voxel counts summarized within manually defined VOIs/ROIs rather than voxelwise stereotactic maps (fails I6 and I9). Because the group-level reporting is effectively ROI/VOI-based, it meets exclusion E3 (reports only ROI results). Therefore it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of analogical reasoning, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed analogy verification requiring planning/relational integration and interference resolution). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults (N=17) using mixed-effects group statistics, with voxelwise results presented in tables and figures and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. BOLD (fMRI) analyses are described in detail. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical, does not report only ROI results, and includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group or clinical comparisons. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in adults that used a block-design block construction/identification task (a variant of the Block Design Task) which the authors explicitly state tests problem-solving/general problem-solving strategies. The paper includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2, normalized to MNI space) and reports within-group task activations for the healthy control group (contrasts vs fixation and condition contrasts). The methods specify use of BOLD EPI acquisition and analyses; stereotactic normalization to MNI space is described and the manuscript refers to activation maps and supplementary materials (where voxelwise coordinate results are provided). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task as defined), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (results in standardized space/MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinate/voxelwise results available in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes a square-completion (visuospatial construction) task that requires a goal and planning/sequencing to determine whether shapes can be assembled into a square, meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses including within-group activations for healthy control subjects (supplemental tables), satisfying I6. BOLD fMRI was used (I8), and results are reported with stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with voxelwise whole-brain statistics (I7). Coordinate results are available in the main text and supplementary materials (I9). Although the sample includes participants with Williams syndrome, the paper provides healthy adult control task effects and whole-brain contrasts, so it is eligible for inclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary data referenced).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=11, mean age 26.9) using auditory multidigit addition (a goal-directed problem-solving task) with blocked task blocks. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates normalized to MNI space (with supplementary tables/figures reporting task-related activations). All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group-only, includes within-healthy-group task effects). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Based on these factors, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=22) that examines relational/relational-integration reasoning across semantic and visuospatial domains. The task constitutes higher-order problem-solving/relational reasoning (goal-directed comparisons requiring integration of relations), meeting the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain GLM results, provides stereotactic (MNI) peak coordinates, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical original data).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults performing a simple mental calculation (X×Y+Z), so it meets I5 (task with a goal needing a method), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the manuscript or tables; activations are shown as figures/voxel maps but no coordinates are provided, so it fails I7 and I9. Because reporting of standardized coordinates is required for inclusion in this coordinate-based meta-analysis, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD-related analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a consistency judgment during text comprehension (“Was the story correct?”), which requires detecting inconsistencies rather than engaging a goal-directed problem-solving process as defined by the review (planning/sequencing actions or executing operations to reach a solution). Therefore it does NOT meet I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, group-comparison-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion IDs met: none.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task involves stroke counting of ideographic characters and motor/visuospatial/lexical retrieval processes rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing to derive a previously unknown solution or critical-thinking operations across domains. The study does meet other methodological criteria: whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6); stereotactic coordinate reporting in MNI/Talairach space (I7); BOLD fMRI analysis (I8); and reporting voxelwise results/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it is excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of series-completion inductive reasoning (number and letter series) in 23 healthy adults. The task requires identifying a rule and generating a solution (goal-directed problem solving), satisfying the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses, BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates (Talairach coordinates are given for ROIs and whole-brain contrasts are described), and provides voxelwise results and ROI confirmatory analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons, empirical healthy-subject task effects reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers using an overt letter verbal fluency task that employs rule-based (phonemic/semantic) search to generate words—meeting the review’s operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-constrained search/planning/execution). The paper reports group-level whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses (GBAMs), provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space, and reports task-related activations in tables/figures. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an event-related, task-based fMRI experiment of solving Chinese logogriphs in healthy adults (meets I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space for the task-related activations (inclusion criterion I7 is not met in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I7).

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates and group- and single-subject analyses, the experimental task is working memory training/maintenance (visuo-spatial WM, digit-span, letter-span) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a solution). The Raven’s Progressive Matrices (a reasoning/problem-solving measure) was administered behaviorally outside the scanner and was not the fMRI task. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task-based fMRI/PET study of a problem-solving task) is not met, even though I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text reviewed. Excluded because the experimental task does not meet I5 (problem-solving) as defined: the task is a social friend/foe judgment and conflict-resolution between verbal and non-verbal cues (social decision-making/theory-of-mind/conflict monitoring), not a goal-directed problem-solving task that requires planning/sequencing operations within an explicit rule framework to arrive at a correct or novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI reported), I9 (coordinates available in main text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, and I9). However, the task is a Shepard–Metzler mental rotation/perceptual matching task, which primarily assesses visuo-spatial transformation/mental imagery rather than a multi-step goal-directed problem-solving process as defined in I5 (evaluating/planning/sequencing actions to reach a solution within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes a mental calculation task (subtraction) which fits the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed manipulation of numerical information using rule-based operations). The study reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise analyses across the imaged brain volume in healthy right-handed adults (n=10), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI. Results are reported voxelwise (with pairwise contrasts and coordinates) rather than ROI-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is a one-back relational judgment (SPACE/TIME/CAUSALITY) with explicit statement that there were no correct answers for individual trials; it does not require setting a goal, planning/sequencing actions to reach a solution, or executing operations to derive a previously unknown correct solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults; random-effects group analyses, N=15), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space in tables/figures), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED due to failure to satisfy I5.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results described and available in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a mental rotation spatial working-memory/visuospatial task, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (participants are adolescents, not healthy adults; group-level effects are not in healthy adult individuals), I7 (while data were normalized to Talairach space, stereotactic coordinates are not explicitly reported in the provided text). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET studies of problem solving in healthy adults.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task used (multisource interference task combined with n-back) probes cognitive control and working memory, not problem-solving as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to discover a previously unknown solution). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates rule-based categorization and category learning. The task involves goal-directed hypothesis testing, rule formation, evaluation, and execution of rule-based decisions to arrive at correct category responses, which fits the review’s operational definition of problem solving (identifying/planning/performing rule-constrained operations to reach a correct solution). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM, BOLD fMRI measures, and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach) in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results as stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for group-level effects. However, the experimental task investigates humor comprehension/incongruity resolution (reading/verbal jokes) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (having a goal and needing to figure out a way to reach it). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of mathematical problem solving in healthy adults (n=39). Methods report whole-brain voxel-wise group-level GLM analyses and state-based MVPA–HMM results based on BOLD fMRI, with significant voxel maps (thresholded voxel-wise) and regional results described; figures/tables are indicated for the voxelwise results. The task fits the defined problem-solving construct (goal-directed algebra-like problem solving). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9.

This is a PET study of verbal fluency (orthographic word generation), not a domain-general problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). Although the task requires internal generation/search, the manuscript frames and assesses it as verbal fluency/language/executive retrieval rather than problem solving across domains. The full text shows whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates (Talairach), and rCBF measures, but it does not meet the meta-analysis’s required task definition (I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of semantic event sequencing requiring subjects to plan and order events (a problem-solving/sequencing task). It uses healthy adult participants (n=12) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise BOLD analyses normalized to MNI space with stereotactic coordinates and corrected statistics; results are presented in tables/figures. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for problem-solving-related sequencing tasks (I5–I9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain BOLD analyses (I6 and I8 satisfied). However, the experimental task is moral judgment of personal/impersonal dilemmas (utilitarian vs deontological decision-making), which is a moral decision-making paradigm rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by the review (no explicit problem structure requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). Therefore I5 (study of a problem-solving task as defined) is not met. Additionally, the provided full text does not explicitly present stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space in the pasted content (I7 not demonstrated) nor explicitly point to coordinate tables in supplements in the provided text (I9 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI investigation of mental rotation in ASD and matched controls and provides group-level activation maps (controls), stereotactic Talairach coordinates, and PPI connectivity results. However, the meta-analysis inclusion requires a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing, and rule-based operations across domains such as semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical). Mental rotation is a visuospatial/perceptual transformation task and does not meet the review definition of problem solving. Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply; the full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults but does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5). The task is a spatial judgement/mental imagery (Mental Clock Test) that requires angle discrimination and attention/imagery processes rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic reporting in standard space / MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results and maps reported/tabled). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per review definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5 not met). It is a methods/rtfMRI validation study using a finger-tapping motor task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results/activation maps indicated in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I7 (the full text does not clearly present stereotactic coordinate tables of task-related increases in Talairach/MNI space). Exclusion criteria met: none []. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objectives and all required inclusion criteria. The task is a goal-directed multi-attribute decision task in which participants must evaluate attributes and apply decision heuristics (rule-based operations) to choose an alternative—meeting the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). The sample comprises healthy adult participants and the analysis uses whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI (I6). Data are analyzed in stereotactic (Talairach) space with reported task-related activations (I7) and the paper reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). Voxelwise results are described and presumably available in tables/figures as part of the main text (I9). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult subjects that includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses reported in Talairach space. The reverse-alphabetizing task is an explicit rule-based ordering/sequencing task (goal: order words in reverse alphabetical order) that requires evaluating stimuli, planning/sequencing actions, and executing operations according to a defined rule set — consistent with the review's definition of a problem-solving task. The study reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI), group ANOVA contrasts, and stereotactic peak activations in PFC (Talairach coordinates), satisfying I6–I8; the task also meets I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses an fMRI similarity-judgment (feature-matching) task rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined in the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a novel/appropriate solution). Although the paper reports whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and indicates voxelwise/parametric maps available in supplemental materials (satisfying I9 and providing evidence toward stereotactic reporting), it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (the task is a perceptual/similarity decision, not a problem-solving task involving planning or complex rule-based solution generation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the paper must be excluded for failure to meet I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=15) that operationalizes a problem-solving/reasoning task (transitive inference) requiring goal-directed manipulation and integration of learned information to derive novel relationships. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using BOLD EPI data, with results referenced to Talairach standardized space and statistical activation maps (tables/figures) of percent signal change. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for a problem-solving task, whole-brain group analysis, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analysis. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study does not investigate problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (I5 not met). It used verbal and non-verbal working memory paradigms rather than tasks requiring goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution operations. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (performed whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses including a healthy control group), I8 (reported BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results presented in figures and voxelwise regression reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is working memory, not problem solving), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not clearly reported in the provided text/tables). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses task-based fMRI of healthy adults performing category learning/classification tasks that require applying learned category rules to determine category membership (i.e., goal-directed rule-based classification), which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving via application of rule sets. It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (mixed-effects ANOVAs), includes voxelwise results and stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space, and reports BOLD percent signal change analyses. Voxelwise/coordinate results are described and tabulated, not limited to ROI-only reporting. Participants are healthy adults and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, disease/age/gender-only comparisons, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy young adults that reports BOLD signal analyses, but the fMRI results are presented using an anatomical region-of-interest (AROI) approach rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group analysis with stereotactic coordinates. Exclusion met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion met: I8 (reports BOLD analysis). Inclusion not met: I5 (the Piaget-like numerical/inhibition task is a perceptual/numerical judgment with inhibitory control rather than a clearly defined multi-step problem-solving task as specified), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/group-level whole-brain analysis reported), I7 (no explicit stereotactic coordinate tables of task-related increases provided in the text; results are given as AROI labels and MNI-space figures but not as coordinate lists), I9 (voxelwise coordinate results are not presented in tables/figures in a way that meets this criterion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported; data normalized to MNI space and Table I reported peak activations), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5 (task is NOT a problem-solving task as defined). The experimental task requires inferring actors' intentions from observed symbolic gestures (social cognition/intent understanding), but does not involve formulating a goal and devising/planning/implementing rule-based operations to reach a solution (e.g., semantic/algebraic/logical problem solving). Therefore it does not meet the review's definition of problem solving. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET/EEG methods paper on verbal creative thinking in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (appears to include whole-brain voxelwise PET analyses using SPM across subjects) and I8 (rCBF PET analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the tasks are creativity/insight and originality tasks—story composition, associative chains, original definitions, proverb sense-flipping—rather than explicit problem-solving tasks defined as goal-directed, rule-based operations with evaluative/planning/execution components to reach a correct solution), and I7 (the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space; although Talairach atlas is mentioned, coordinate tables or voxel coordinates are not presented in the provided content). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (core sections present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the problem-solving task definition (I5) and does not provide stereotactic coordinates (I7).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain BOLD analyses normalized to Talairach space, so it meets I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the experimental paradigm is a morality Implicit Association Test (IAT) probing implicit moral attitudes and response conflict, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

The study is excluded because participants are adolescents (mean ages 16.8 and 16.9), not healthy adults as required by inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI mental-rotation task meeting the review’s problem-solving definition), I7 (task-related stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires healthy adult participants; sample is adolescent). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the report. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a visuospatial relative judgment (compare dot-bar distance to a reference line) that primarily assesses perceptual/attentional processing and relative comparison, not higher-order problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing, or executing operations within a rule set to arrive at a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (a rule-based, goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing and executing operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (N=26), uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (peaks and ROI coordinates). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not clinical-group-only, not non-empirical).

This is a behavioral study of arithmetic (reaction times and strategy ratings) in healthy adults; it does not include any task-based fMRI or PET data, whole-brain group-level analyses, stereotactic coordinates, or BOLD/rCBF results. Full text is complete. Exclusion rationale: No imaging modalities or voxelwise results reported. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI or PET study), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analysis), I9 (not applicable—no voxelwise results to report). Exclusion criteria met: none of the listed exclusion IDs (E3–E6) directly apply; exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET problem-solving studies.

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (I5). The tasks reported are perceptual classification (/ra/-/la/) and nonsymbolic magnitude comparison (numerical distance-effect), which are decision/perception tasks rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving planning, sequencing, or applying rule-based operations to arrive at novel solutions. The paper does include whole-brain BOLD analyses in healthy adults (satisfying I6 and I8), and presents voxelwise results/figures (I9), but it does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) in the provided full text (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I7 while meeting I6, I8, and I9.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The fMRI tasks are theory-of-mind (False-Belief and Person-Description) mental-state reasoning and emotion/appearance judgments, not goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a solution as specified in I5. It does, however, satisfy other methodological criteria: whole-brain task-based fMRI with group-level effects (I6), stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space (I7), BOLD fMRI measurements (I8), and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, exclude because inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task per meta-analysis definition) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

The study uses a free word association / inhibition task in mood disorder patients and healthy controls, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct solution; instead it probes semantic association and inhibition). Thus I5 is not met. The full text is complete and provides whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), includes BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and presents voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore exclude on the basis of failing I5.

I exclude because the study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The tasks are auditory sentence comprehension and Shepard-Metzler mental rotation; these are language comprehension and visuospatial transformation tasks rather than goal-directed problem-solving as defined (tasks requiring planning/sequencing/executing operations within a rule set to reach a correct or novel solution). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports results in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

The study is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adult participants performing arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) that require goal-directed calculation and sequential rule-based operations, meeting the review's problem-solving definition. It used group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses, reported BOLD fMRI contrasts, and provided stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task = mental calculation, a problem-solving-like task with goal and method), I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI was performed in nine healthy adults), I8 (fMRI BOLD sequence and task-related fMRI analysis were reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (the paper does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space — no coordinate tables or coordinate reporting are present in the full text provided), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results are reported in tables, figures, or supplements as required). Because I7 (and I9) are required and are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study is an fMRI case-control investigation of visual imagery (face perception and imagery) in a patient with loss of imagery versus healthy controls. Although it includes whole-brain BOLD analyses with group-level effects in healthy adults (controls) and indicates voxelwise results are reported, the experimental tasks are visual perception and imagery, not problem-solving as defined in the review (no goal-directed planning, sequencing, logical or semantic rule-based operations to discover unknown solutions). Therefore it fails the key inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is not demonstrably met in the provided text (coordinate tables/values are not present in the supplied content), though the paper likely contains cluster tables; I6 and I8 are satisfied and I9 is plausibly satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Hence EXCLUDED because I5 not met (and I7 not clearly met).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, but the experimental tasks are magnitude-comparison judgments (numerical, luminance, size) rather than problem-solving as defined by the review (requires goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a novel solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task per the review's definition) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standardized space), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise/contrast results presented in maps/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of moral reasoning (personal/impersonal dilemmas) in healthy older adults and bvFTD patients. It includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) reported. However, it does not study a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or executing operations within a rule set to arrive at a correct/novel solution); moral dilemma deliberation is not operationalized as the specified problem-solving types. Therefore I5 is not met. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5.)

The study uses an object recognition/visuospatial paradigm in older adults (aMCI patients and controls) rather than a defined problem-solving task as required by I5. Although the study reports task-based BOLD fMRI (I8 satisfied), it does not meet the review’s core requirement that the task be a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Additionally, the provided full text does not clearly present stereotactic peak coordinates in Talairach/MNI space (I7 not met) and does not provide demonstrable whole-brain, significant group-level task effects in healthy adults suitable for inclusion (I6 not met). I9 (availability of voxelwise results in tables/figures) is not clearly satisfied in the supplied text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) from the review are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly contrasts well-structured problem-solving and ill-structured design tasks. The problem-solving condition fits the review's definition (explicit goal, legal moves, unique solutions). The paper reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses using SPM5 with family-wise error correction, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents voxelwise results. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I9) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a modified beads (probabilistic reasoning) task where participants have the goal (identify lake source) and must determine how to reach it (decide how many samples to draw) — meeting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and event-related contrasts in healthy adults, with stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations (e.g., VTA [3 −25 −11], VS [12 8 −8]) and reports BOLD fMRI results. Results are presented in the main text with coordinates and ROI analyses supplementing whole-brain findings. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used a rule-based manipulation task (alphabetical reordering of letters) that requires planning/sequencing and execution of operations to arrive at a correct response, fitting the review's problem-solving definition. Participants were healthy adults; analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise BOLD fMRI using SPM, with results reported as stereotactic coordinates (tables/figures) in standard space (MNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion with coordinate tables and figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=13) where participants performed a goal-directed visuospatial problem-solving task (assemble three shapes into a namable composite) versus a control mental-rotation task, satisfying the review’s definition of problem solving (goal, planning/manipulation, execution to produce a solution). Whole-brain group-level analysis was performed (FLAME mixed-effects), results are thresholded and reported with stereotactic MNI coordinates (Table 1/figures), and BOLD fMRI analyses are used. All required reporting formats are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison-only, empirical healthy-group task effects are reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of complex working memory span (CWMS), not a problem-solving task as defined for this review. Although it uses whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates, it does not involve tasks that require goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or executing rule-based steps to arrive at novel solutions. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available in main text/supplement). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 (task-based study of problem solving as defined). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not meet the required conceptual scope of a problem-solving task.

This is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14) investigating quantitative reasoning (perimeter comparison) that requires rule-based evaluation and inhibitory control to resolve conflict—meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving across domains. The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses normalized to MNI space with stereotactic coordinates, and voxelwise task-related activation results. All relevant inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only between-group disease/age/gender comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Tower of London planning task, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing). It reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (healthy participants), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (MNI, with Talairach conversion) for task-related activations. All inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete and appropriate for inclusion.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). It uses an auditory n-back verbal working memory task (maintenance/updating), which does not require goal-directed problem decomposition, planning/sequencing of actions, or rule-based solution generation typical of problem-solving paradigms. The full text is complete. The study does, however, satisfy multiple other inclusion criteria: it is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study with group-level effects in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and presents voxelwise results available in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded solely because it fails I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Brixton rule-attainment task requiring participants to infer and apply rules (goal-directed problem solving: identify rules, generate hypotheses, and execute responses). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses of BOLD fMRI data, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for activations in tables/figures, and includes voxelwise results. Thus it meets inclusion I5 (problem-solving/rule inference and application), I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines goal-directed, strategic decision-making in economic games (prisoner’s dilemma and stag hunt). The tasks require participants to evaluate options, plan/implement strategies (iterative reasoning/dominance-solvable computations), and execute rule-based decisions to maximize payoff, consistent with the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses (cluster-corrected), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion: none of the exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level whole-sample PET analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (regional cerebral blood flow PET analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion not met: I5 (task is a verbal memory/semantic-organization encoding paradigm and measures strategy use during recall, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review—there is no explicit requirement to identify and perform critical-thinking operations to devise a solution to a presented problem across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule frameworks). Full text appears complete.

This study used task-based BOLD fMRI of healthy adults during a probabilistic inference (jumping-to-conclusions) task, so it meets I5 (task involves a goal and iterative evidence-gathering to reach it) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). However, the paper reports ROI-based multivariate analyses (DLPFC, ACC, OFC, hippocampus, etc.) rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis with stereotactic coordinates. No Talairach/MNI coordinate tables or whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are provided in the full text. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results) and does not meet inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis) or I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates). I9 (availability of voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based primarily on E3 plus failure to meet I6 and I7.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16) that examines analogical reasoning requiring subjects to generate representations and map source to target to choose a correct target (i.e., a goal-directed problem-solving process). The paper includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, reports task-related BOLD effects, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (multiple BA10 peaks and other regions). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based neuroimaging studies of problem solving (I5–I9). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group-level analyses, BOLD results, and stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standardized space), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available). However, it does not meet I5: the experimental tasks probe verbal working memory manipulation and monitoring (reordering items according to a previously learned sequence) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring identification/evaluation/planning to arrive at a previously unknown solution across domains). No exclusion criteria are triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) during a fluid reasoning/problem-solving task (Raven’s/matrix reasoning and an fMRI reasoning vs control task) in a large sample of healthy young adults (n=109 for fMRI; overall n=225). Analyses included whole-brain, voxelwise group-level correlations between activation and intelligence measures and ROI definition based on those voxelwise maps (figures and text describe voxelwise thresholding at p<0.001). The paper explicitly references figures and supplemental tables/figures (supplemental Tables/Figs) documenting the imaging results, indicating stereotactic/voxelwise results are available in the main/ supplemental materials.
