Thus the study meets inclusion I5 (task qualifies as problem-solving/reasoning), I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (voxelwise/stereotactic results indicated in figures/supplement), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/supplement acceptable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Confidence lowered slightly because explicit coordinate tables are not shown in the provided excerpt but are signposted as supplemental material.

This is a task-based fMRI study of relational reasoning/transitive inference in healthy adult participants that involves logical problem-solving operations (deriving comparative relations and planning/sequencing to infer novel relations), meeting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (FLAME) with cluster-corrected results in MNI space and provides BOLD effects. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical data).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a transitive reasoning task (logical problem-solving). It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses (n=17) with BOLD fMRI, uses MNI normalization and reports stereotactic coordinates (e.g., 42,20,-8), and reports task-related activation results in the main text. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This study does not meet the review objective for problem-solving in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI analysis is reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is an n-back visuospatial working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (while whole-brain group analyses are reported, the participant sample is mixed-age with minors and clinical Fragile X subjects; it does not report whole-brain, group-level effects exclusively in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates are not explicitly provided in the supplied text despite Talairach normalization being described). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) were directly triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants performing verbal fluency tasks (phonological, lexical, semantic). The verbal fluency tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition: each has a clear goal (generate words meeting a rule) and requires strategic retrieval, planning/sequencing, and rule-constrained operations (semantic/category, initial-letter, rhyme constraints). Group-level whole-brain results are reported (FDR-corrected), coordinates are provided/transformed into Talairach/MNI space, and BOLD analyses are described. Although a pharmacological manipulation (S-ketamine vs placebo) was included, the participants are healthy adults and task-related healthy-group effects (task>baseline during placebo and ketamine, and KET>PLA contrasts) are reported, so the study provides usable whole-brain coordinates for problem-solving (semantic/lexical) tasks. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement learning) task rather than an explicit problem-solving task. While the task involves obtaining rewards and adapting behavior, it primarily probes model-free/model-based learning and prediction error signaling, not higher-order problem solving or planning per se. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results referenced in main/supplementary materials). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task does not clearly constitute a problem-solving task as defined—having a goal and requiring subjects to figure out a way to reach it in the sense of complex problem solving across domains). No exclusion criteria were directly triggered (e.g., results are not ROI-only, the sample is healthy adults, and the paper is empirical). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving using the Tower of London planning task in 24 healthy adults. It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses (random-effects ANOVA), with results normalized to MNI space and peak coordinates reported. The paper explicitly examines planning/internalization processes (problem solving) and includes voxelwise whole-brain results (with VOI follow-ups). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). The paper reports task-based BOLD fMRI using an n-back working memory paradigm and focuses on working memory capacity, training effects, and comparisons between healthy controls and schizophrenic patients; this is not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults are reported) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is working memory, not problem-solving) and I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not clearly reported in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the available content. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15) that examines goal-directed design (book-cover illustration) involving generation, evaluation, planning, and execution of creative solutions. The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition: participants had an explicit goal and engaged in processes of idea generation, evaluation, and planning to represent concepts visually. The study reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses, BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (multiple peak coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, empirical healthy-group task effects are present). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (the study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review). The task is the "Reading the Mind in the Eyes" mental state decoding/theory-of-mind task (social–perceptual inference), not a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations within a rule set to arrive at a (previously unknown) solution. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I5 while meeting the other technical inclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI investigation of planning/problem-solving (Tower of London visuospatial planning and autobiographical goal-directed planning), meeting the review objective. It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses in 20 healthy adults, uses MNI normalization and reports voxelwise results (PLS clusters and seed coordinates), and includes BOLD-based activation and task-related functional connectivity analyses. Results are reported in stereotactic space and voxelwise findings are presented (with tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not group-comparison-only, includes healthy task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving as defined by the review (I5 not met). It instead investigates theory-of-mind processes (cooperation vs. deception) using cartoon stories requiring belief/intention attribution, not tasks with an explicit goal and requirement to figure out a way to reach it. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults; n=13, random-effects analyses), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates / peak voxels; MNI/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (task-related voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental rotation (participants decide whether paired 3D objects are the same or mirror images), which constitutes a goal-directed visuospatial problem-solving task involving mental transformation and decision-making. The sample is healthy adult participants (right-handed females, 20–30 yrs). Whole-brain group-level analyses were performed (group brain activation maps), stereotactic coordinates of activation foci are reported, and BOLD/T2*-weighted fMRI (rCBF/BOLD contrasts and SSQ-ratio maps) are analyzed and reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, clinical-group-only contrasts, non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving/mental rotation task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD/rCBF analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures/tables).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study including healthy adult participants performing symbolic exact and approximate calculation tasks that meet the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations within an algebraic framework). The study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in adults, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach) for task-related activations, and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is a PET FDG investigation of numerical calculation tasks in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based PET using numerical calculations that fit the review’s problem-solving definition) and I6 (whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses in healthy adults). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I8 (study uses FDG-PET measuring glucose metabolism, not BOLD fMRI or rCBF measures required by the review) and I7 (the paper does not report stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases in brain activation—the reported coordinates refer to baseline BMI correlations, not task-activation coordinates). I9 (acceptable reporting of voxelwise results) is not satisfied for the task-activation contrast because coordinates for task increases are not provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I7 and I8).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used BOLD imaging and whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects GLM). Participants performed spatial memory/imagery tasks (REF, ROT, JRD) that require an explicit goal (point to a cued object) and transformation/mental-reasoning to determine the response, meeting the review definition of problem solving (goal plus need to figure out how to reach it). The functional data were normalized to Talairach space and the manuscript reports task-related activations with referenced tables/figures of voxelwise stereotactic coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study uses an event-related mental arithmetic (complex math) task that requires goal-directed operations under rule-based procedures (algebraic/arithmetical problem solving), i.e., a problem-solving paradigm. It reports whole-brain group-level fMRI (BOLD) analyses in healthy adult participants, with data transformed to MNI space and detailed region results indicated (implying stereotactic coordinate reporting in tables/figures). The methods and results sections are complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of Tower of London problem-solving in healthy adults, meeting the review objective. It reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8) and uses group-level, random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with SPM and FWE correction (I6). Data were normalized to MNI space and activated areas were thresholded and rendered on a template brain, indicating stereotactic (MNI) reporting of task-related increases (I7); voxelwise results are indicated as available in figures/tables (I9). The task clearly involves goal-directed planning and execution consistent with the problem-solving definition (I5). The study is an fMRI investigation of verbal fluency in healthy adults and meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults, coordinate reporting in standardized space, and BOLD fMRI results). Specifically, it satisfies I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, it does NOT meet I5: the experiment uses a verbal fluency (word-generation) task, which is an executive/language task but does not match the review's definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct/novel solution across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it fails to satisfy I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes healthy control participants and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in Talairach space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental tasks are N-back (working memory) and overt verbal fluency (word generation/executive function), which do not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution within a specified rule set). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

Excluded because the task (phonological verbal fluency/word generation) does not meet the review's predefined definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is ineligible solely because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review.

This PET study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. The task (verbal mental-operation) involves a clear goal (advance the day of the week) and rule-based sequential operations to reach a correct answer, satisfying I5 (problem-solving-like task involving planning/sequencing and rule execution). It includes whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses with healthy adult controls (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates referenced to standard space (MNI/Talairach) and tabulated peak activations (I7), and reports rCBF PET results (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures and supplementary materials (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults but does not examine 'problem-solving' as defined by the review (a goal with a need to figure out a way to reach it). It instead studies theory-of-mind/self-perspective inhibition using movie clips and stop-signal tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adult subjects), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/peak coordinates reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not address the target cognitive domain (problem-solving).

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It investigates implicit false-belief/theory-of-mind processing using fMRI and eye-tracking (a social-cognitive anticipatory-looking paradigm), not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (task-based fMRI, whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results are reported/available). Not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task as defined). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of metaphor comprehension/analogical mapping in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses and stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. However, the experimental task is language comprehension (interpreting nominal metaphors within sentence contexts) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., a task with an explicit goal followed by planning/sequencing/executing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution). Therefore it fails to meet I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). It examines perceptual judgments (context-dependent vs context-independent line-length judgments) and temperament moderation of neural responses, not goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. The full text is complete. It does meet several other inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with whole-brain group-level analyses (I6), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and presents voxelwise/cluster results in figures/analyses consistent with acceptable reporting (I9). The manuscript does not present a problem-solving paradigm (I5) and does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates in the provided text (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclude.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The task is a parity (mirror-normal) judgment involving mental rotation and perceptual discrimination/mental imagery, not a problem-solving paradigm as defined (i.e., having a goal and requiring planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations to arrive at a novel solution). The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The paper is a task-based group fMRI study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates, but it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The experimental tasks are rhyme judgment and mental word reversal focused on auditory imagery/phonological manipulation and working memory. Although word reversal requires cognitive transformation, the authors frame it as manipulation of auditory imagery and phonological/visuospatial strategies rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution. Therefore I5 is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation of arithmetic problem solving including healthy adults and children and reports group-level adult results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (arithmetic problem solving satisfies problem-solving definition), I6 (group-level effects in healthy adult participants using task fMRI/GLM), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the main text, figures, or visible tables; criterion I7 is not satisfied based on the material given. Although the paper refers to Supplementary Information, no explicit coordinate tables are present in the provided content and the allowance in I9 (that coordinates may be in supplementary materials) cannot be confirmed here. Per screening rules, ALL inclusion criteria must be met; because I7 is not demonstrated in the provided full text, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the supplied content.

This fMRI study investigates retrieval of action knowledge (how vs why actions are performed) using a covert recall task; it does not involve problem-solving as defined (a goal followed by figuring out a way to reach it or engaging planning/sequencing to derive a solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. The study does meet other methodological criteria (task-based whole-brain fMRI with group-level analyses, stereotactic MNI coordinates reported, and BOLD analyses), but because it does not study a problem-solving task, it must be excluded.

Excluded (E3): the study reports ROI-based analyses rather than a whole-brain voxelwise whole-brain group analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is discourse comprehension/inference generation, not a defined problem-solving task as required), I6 (no whole-brain analysis with group-level whole-brain effects; analyses were constrained to a priori ROIs), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI space are not reported). Full text appears complete and does not change these determinations.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults that used whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5), reported BOLD effects with MNI coordinates, and provided voxelwise results: it therefore meets I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the experimental paradigm is passive sentence reading manipulating referential ambiguity/failure and semantic anomaly; participants were instructed to read for comprehension (no explicit goal-directed problem-solving instructions or a task requiring planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct solution). Although authors interpret referential ambiguity as engaging inference/problem-solving, the study does not implement a bona fide problem-solving task as defined in I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is moral decision-making/social judgment (judging acceptability of actions in vignettes) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. It does, however, satisfy several methodological inclusion criteria: it is a whole-brain task-based fMRI study with group-level analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for task-related increases (I7), includes BOLD analyses (I8), and voxelwise results are available in text/tables/supplementary materials (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude for failing I5.

This is a task-based BOLD-fMRI study of two-digit mental addition (choice-reaction), which meets the review's problem-solving definition (a goal to indicate the correct result and the need to compute/figure out the result). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants (N=16 after exclusion), normalized to MNI space, and provides voxelwise stereotactic coordinates and parametric contrasts. BOLD signal (fMRI) analyses are reported, with tables/figures and detailed voxelwise results. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study using BOLD whole-brain analyses comparing medicated schizophrenia patients and matched healthy controls during a sensorimotor/tactile prediction task. It meets I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects including healthy adults), I7 (data normalized to MNI space and results reported with region foci/eTable), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results referenced in figures/supplement). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is a sensorimotor prediction/tactile attenuation paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed reasoning/planning/sequencing to derive a solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet the essential inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

This study does not meet the review’s core eligibility. It is an fMRI task study with whole-brain MNI coordinates and BOLD analyses (satisfies I7, I8, I9). However, it does not study a problem-solving task as defined (task is letter/location discrimination, not goal-directed problem solving) and participants are male adolescents (ages 11–16) including an ADHD clinical group rather than healthy adults (fails I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

I5 not met: The study investigates sustained task-set maintenance and cognitive control across three tasks (coherence discrimination, mental rotation, noun/verb classification). These do not clearly constitute 'problem-solving' as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to discover or execute a solution within a rule set to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results/figures reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it does not meet I5.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a 3-operand mental arithmetic task (goal-directed calculation following rule-based operations), which qualifies as a problem-solving task per the review definition. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5 second-level analyses) in a healthy adult sample (N=49), uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI and transformed Talairach) for task-related activations/deactivations. Voxelwise results are reported and ROI analyses supplement but do not replace whole-brain results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the main adaptation experiment involved passive viewing of numerosities, the study also includes an event-related functional localizer in which healthy adult participants performed mental calculation (subtraction) versus sentence comprehension. The authors report random-effects, whole-brain group-level contrasts (calculation > sentence) with stereotactic coordinates and BOLD fMRI analyses (coordinates and cluster-level thresholds are given). Participants were healthy adults. Therefore the paper contains a task that meets the review's problem-solving definition (mental calculation requiring goal-directed operations), includes whole-brain group analyses, reports stereotactic coordinates, and reports BOLD results. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (pyramid problems) in healthy adult participants that examines neural activity during problem solution and learning. It includes group-level whole-brain analyses (exploratory voxelwise contrasts identifying metacognitive and cognitive regions) and predefined ROI and whole-brain results. Stereotactic Talairach coordinates are reported for predefined regions and exploratory loci. The imaging modality is BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are described and presented in figures/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review; it examines moral judgment/Theory of Mind, not goal-directed problem-solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based operations to reach a solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (N=316) that examines goal-directed semantic judgments (living/nonliving) including an ambiguous (hard) condition that requires deliberative evaluation and decision-making. The ambiguous condition entails evaluative/critical thinking processes to categorize items under a semantic rule set, consistent with the review's broad definition of problem solving (semantic rule-based decision-making). The study reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results, and includes the relevant contrasts (easy vs. fixation; hard vs. easy) with tables/figures of coordinates. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is a semantic decision/judgment task (deciding whether nouns designate objects available in a supermarket and cost less than a threshold), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (lacking goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to derive a previously unknown solution). (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task is semantic decision, not problem-solving). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based PET study using a problem-solving paradigm (modified Tower of London) meeting the review definition of problem solving. It includes healthy adult control participants and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory 3-D Gaussian random field theory thresholding) and ROI analyses. Task-related rCBF (PET) results are reported with stereotactic coordinates (x,y,z) and Brodmann areas, and task effects in healthy controls are described (within-group learning-related decreases) as well as comparisons between controls and patients. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in standardized (MNI) space; however the experimental task targets prospective memory (performing real-world errands in VR) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (explicitly requiring subjects to formulate and figure out ways to reach a goal). Although the VR PM task involves goal-directed behavior and navigation, the paper frames and analyzes processes as prospective memory components (intention maintenance, target detection, action, switching) rather than domain-general problem solving. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not met, while I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. It examines moral sensitivity, empathy, and intentionality using viewing tasks (moral scenarios), not goal-directed problem solving or tasks requiring planning/sequencing to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task-based whole-brain fMRI with group-level effects, including analyses of adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria applied: none of E3–E6 are met. Full text appears complete. Consequently, the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

Full text is complete. This study does NOT meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is an AX-CPT continuous performance paradigm probing attention, cognitive set bias, and reward expectancy during target detection, monitoring, and rule-following, but not problem-solving as defined (no requirement to identify/plan novel solutions or perform higher-order problem evaluation/planning to reach a previously unknown solution). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are violated). Thus excluded because I5 is not met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines mental arithmetic (complex multiplication and division) involving goal-directed problem solving to arrive at previously unknown numerical solutions. The methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM, with reporting of stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD-based fMRI (EPI) results. The paper includes full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem-solving arithmetic task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons only, empirical original data). Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study administered the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST), which requires establishing a goal (match cards) and discovering/adjusting rules to reach it, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses for healthy adult controls (single-group results and group comparisons) (I6). Task-related increases are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (tables/figures referenced; z coordinate of Talairach space noted) (I7). BOLD fMRI was used and analyzed (I8). Voxelwise and clusterwise results are presented in tables and figures in the main text, consistent with acceptable reporting (I9). Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Although the study is a task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain group analyses (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD/fMRI analyses with coordinates reported (I8,I9), it does not investigate a 'problem-solving' task per the review's I5 definition. The tasks are mental rotation and silent reading/recognition, aimed at manipulating cognitive context and semantic processing rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used a 2-back verbal working-memory task (not a problem-solving task as defined by I5) and reports group differences using averaged activation within 8 a priori ROIs rather than providing whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps or stereotactic coordinates. It therefore does not meet the review's requirements for a whole-brain, task-based problem-solving study with coordinate-based results. Inclusion met: I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion not met: I5 (task is working memory, not a defined problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results for task-related increases). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results) and E5 (does not provide healthy-group whole-brain task effects / reports only between-group contrasts within ROIs). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of transitive inference (a goal-directed reasoning/problem-solving task requiring relational integration). It tested 16 healthy adult participants, reports whole-brain group-level analyses (GLM, group t tests), provides stereotactic coordinates for activation peaks, and describes BOLD fMRI methods and results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (no-only-ROI results, no patient-group-only contrasts, and it is not a review). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines reasoning/problem-solving across two domains (temperature and poverty) where participants must evaluate choices and report confidence (goal-directed reasoning/critical thinking). The methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, BOLD fMRI acquisition, and provide stereotactic coordinates in standardized space (ICBM/MNI). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies I5 (problem-solving reasoning task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results presented). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses a Tower of London planning task (a problem-solving paradigm requiring goal identification, planning/sequencing of moves, and execution) in healthy adult controls and medication-free OCD patients. It reports whole-brain, random-effects SPM analyses (group-level main effects for controls and group contrasts), task-related BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates referenced to Talairach space in multiple tables. The paper is empirical, includes healthy adult task effects, and does not limit results to ROIs. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review's problem-solving definition (I5). This is an fMRI n-back working memory study (identity match and magnitude/comparison of single items) rather than a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach an unknown solution. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is working memory/comparison, not problem solving as defined). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI with group-level analyses including healthy adults (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). However, the experimental task is a verbal fluency (word generation) paradigm, which is a language/executive-production task and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met: task is not defined as goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a novel solution). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

Excluded because the task (overt verbal fluency) does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met): it is primarily a language/executive retrieval task rather than requiring explicit goal-directed planning/sequencing operations across a rule-based problem to arrive at a novel solution. The paper does satisfy I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables). It does not provide a whole-brain, group-level task effect reported for healthy adults alone (I6 not met) and mainly reports combined group task effects and between-group contrasts; thus it meets exclusion E5 (no healthy-group task effect / effectively only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that includes classic problem-solving/fluid-reasoning tasks (Paper Folding, Matrix Reasoning, Letter Sets) and reports BOLD-based GLM group analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (problem-solving tasks), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD analysis). However, the provided full text does not present task-related stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) in the excerpt; although imaging was performed in MNI space and RANN maps/images are described, no coordinate tables or explicit stereotactic coordinates are included in the supplied content. Therefore I7 (reporting of stereotactic coordinate results) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Based on the requirement that ALL inclusion criteria must be met, I exclude this study.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inferential reasoning (exclusion), which constitutes logical problem-solving (subjects infer relations and select a correct novel comparison based on learned rules), satisfying I5. The study used healthy adult participants (n=15) and reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses in standardized space (Talairach normalization described), satisfying I6 and I7. BOLD fMRI was used and task-related contrasts (Exclusion > Baseline; S+ > Baseline) are reported, satisfying I8. The manuscript presents voxelwise activation results and refers to figures/cluster locations, consistent with I9 (voxelwise results available in main text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, empirical healthy-subject task effects reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is INCLUDED.

This task-based fMRI study explicitly manipulates mechanical problem solving by asking healthy adults to plan and execute pantomimes for unfamiliar tools (requiring function-from-structure inference) and compares these with familiar-tool pantomimes. It reports whole-brain group-level analyses, voxelwise stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space, and BOLD fMRI results (including tables/figures of activation). Thus it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task via mechanical reasoning), I6 (whole-brain group effects in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses a covert verbal initiation (Hayling sentence completion) task that requires a goal (complete the sentence) and semantic problem solving to select an appropriate completion, meeting the review’s operational definition of problem solving (semantic domain). It reports whole‑brain, voxelwise, group‑level random effects fMRI analyses (SPM99) including within‑group maps for healthy control adults, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and reports BOLD fMRI results in tables/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI‑only, not a review, includes healthy group task effects). Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and is INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study with healthy adult participants that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in standardized (MNI) space and provides coordinate tables and figures (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental tasks are allocentric/egocentric spatial judgments and a luminance discrimination baseline; these are perceptual/spatial judgment tasks, not problem-solving tasks as defined (i.e., having a goal and requiring planning, sequencing, or executing operations to reach a novel solution). Therefore it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This task-based fMRI study (healthy adult volunteers, N=14) used the PASAT, which requires goal-directed arithmetic operations (adding consecutive digits according to explicit rules) and thus fits the review definition of a problem-solving task (rule-based, goal-oriented operations). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, BOLD fMRI data, and stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach) with coordinate tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, tables/figures referenced) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Note: sample size is modest (14), which may limit generalizability but does not violate inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of moral evaluation and justice sensitivity, not a problem-solving task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does NOT employ a problem-solving task as defined; the task involves moral evaluation of observed actions, praise/blame ratings, and mentalizing, rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis because it fails to meet I5.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults and reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results, but it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a task with an explicit goal that requires figuring out a way to reach it). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task; it examines sentential negation/language comprehension). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, no patient-only or between-group-only contrasts, empirical data present). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails I5.

The study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving as defined in inclusion criterion I5. The task is social prediction/impression-formation (theory-of-mind vs deontic reasoning) and involves learning/prediction about others’ behavior, but does not require participants to set a goal and plan/execute operations to solve a problem in the sense of critical thinking/planning/sequencing to reach a solution. The full text is complete. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and voxelwise results are reported (I9). This empirical task-based fMRI study includes the Tower of London task, a canonical problem-solving/planning paradigm (I5). It reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (normalized to MNI space) with task-related activation maps and contrasts (whole-brain FDR-corrected maps), and provides region coordinates (e.g., caudate coordinates) and post hoc group comparisons involving healthy controls (fulfilling I6 and I7). BOLD fMRI was used (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text (I9). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, and is sufficiently complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI results (it includes whole-brain SPM), is not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore it is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of whole-brain, task-based fMRI studies of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This study is excluded because it reports only an a priori ROI analysis rather than whole-brain stereotactic coordinate results (exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a working-memory n-Back, which does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task), I6 (no clear whole-brain group-level coordinate-based analysis is reported — results are presented from ROIs), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases are reported in the text), I9 (no coordinates in main text, tables, figures or supplement are provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study used a simple number-reading/identification task (number naming/press corresponding button) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no evidence of goal-directed planning, sequencing, or solution-generation operations). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not meet the review’s definition of problem solving). I7 (stereotactic coordinates) are not clearly reported in the provided full text (BA labels and Talairach normalization are mentioned but coordinate tables/values are not shown), so I7 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) appear to apply. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates causal inference and contextual analysis during causal-attribution tasks, which require subjects to infer causes of events—an inferential/critical-thinking process consistent with the review’s definition of problem-solving (I5). It reports whole-brain group-level random-effects SPM analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in the main text/tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: the study includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only) and reports within-group task effects in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using problem-solving tasks (NSI and OSI) where participants had a goal and had to figure out methods to reach it (I5). The paper reports whole-brain group-level random-effects GLM analyses in healthy university adults (I6), with results transformed into Talairach space and peak coordinates reported (I7). BOLD fMRI was used and analyzed (I8). Voxelwise task effects and coordinates are reported in figures/tables and correlations with behavior are presented (I9). The study does not rely solely on ROIs, does not report only group comparisons of disease/age/gender, and includes healthy-group task effects, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=15) using an anagram problem-solving paradigm that requires goal-directed generate-and-evaluate operations, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2 (I6), with stereotactic coordinates referenced to the MNI template reported for task-related increases (I7). It uses BOLD fMRI (I8) and provides voxelwise coordinate results in the main text (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not disease/age/gender comparisons only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (multi-digit addition), which constitutes a problem-solving task (goal-directed computation). It reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses in healthy adult participants, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and includes voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group comparisons only, empirical healthy-sample task effects present).

The study uses an object-recall-from-features semantic memory task (deciding whether two feature words evoke a specific object). While it employs whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level random-effects analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates, the task is primarily semantic retrieval/recognition rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review (i.e., having an explicit goal that requires planning/sequencing or executing operations to derive a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet the review's problem-solving inclusion criterion (I5). It does meet I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: E3 and E5. The study is an fMRI BOLD study (I8 met) but does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met), does not report whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults (I6 not met), and does not report stereotactic coordinates from a whole-brain analysis (I7 not met). Instead, the analysis is restricted to pre-defined regions of interest (ROI-only analysis), and results are presented as ROI BOLD magnitudes rather than voxelwise whole-brain coordinates (meets exclusion E3). The paper focuses on bipolar patients with lithium treatment and lacks a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (meets exclusion E5). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, (I9 not applicable). Therefore the study should be excluded from the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=15) using a goal-directed, rule-based landing decision task that requires evaluating the problem, planning, and executing actions (land vs. go-around), fitting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (SPM8) with BOLD fMRI, provides stereotactic coordinates converted to Talairach space, and reports cluster results and ROI/SVC analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, non-empirical paper, or lack of healthy-group task effects) are met.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Korean and American adults) that reports voxelwise BOLD results in standardized space (MNI) with group-level analyses and stereotactic coordinates. The task (moral dilemmas) requires goal-directed evaluation and critical thinking (weighing outcomes, planning/choosing actions to achieve goals, utilitarian vs deontological reasoning), which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (evaluating a problem and deciding/choosing actions to satisfy goals). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a number-bisection task that requires applying rules and magnitude computations to decide whether the central number is the interval mean—i.e., goal-directed problem solving involving rule-based operations and evaluation. The study conducted whole-brain, random-effects group analyses and reports voxelwise activation results with Talairach coordinates. BOLD-sensitive fMRI (rBOLD) was used and multiple parametric contrasts are reported. Therefore it meets I5 (problem-solving/task requiring rule-based operations), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-only or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not address the review objective of problem-solving in healthy adults. It is a methods paper using task-based fMRI to predict/ classify disorders (cocaine use, schizophrenia, Alzheimer’s) versus controls. Although whole-brain BOLD analyses and stereotactic coordinates are reported, the primary contrasts and results are group classification (patient vs control) rather than within-group healthy adult task effects reflecting problem-solving processes. The tasks used are varied (sensorimotor, oddball, working memory, reward paradigms, flicker/checkerboard; a ‘calculations’ condition exists only in the Fast Acquisition dataset used as a stability check), but the paper does not test or report task-related problem-solving activations in healthy adults across domains. Therefore it fails inclusion I5 (problem-solving task) and I6 (study reports group-level healthy adult task effects). It meets I7 (coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates available in text/figures). It also meets exclusion E5 (focus on between-group classification and lacks healthy-group task effects).

This PET study used a task of serial subtraction (mental calculation), which qualifies as a problem-solving task (rule-based arithmetic operations to arrive at correct answers). It includes healthy adult participants (n=6) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (normalized to a standard stereotaxic atlas), showing task-related activations within the healthy group as well as in patients. Regional CBF was measured (H2 15O PET), satisfying the rCBF/BOLD requirement. The paper indicates voxel-wise SPM results (voxel coordinates/results are presented in voxel-based analyses and likely in figures/tables), meeting the reporting requirements for standardized-space stereotactic results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI task study in healthy adults but does NOT investigate an explicit problem-solving task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in stereotactic space, MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — participants observed videos of stone toolmaking and either imagined or evaluated actions; they were not required to identify/plan/execute solutions to a novel problem or perform goal-directed problem solving per the review definition. No exclusion criteria applied (none met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude for failing I5.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The tasks are self-construal priming (pronoun detection) and subsequent resting-state scans; the priming tasks are target-detection/semantic-priming and not goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution. Although there is an intervening calculation task, it serves as a baseline and is not the primary experimental manipulation nor described as a problem-solving paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based problem-solving). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes an arithmetic task (Reverse Polish notation) requiring goal-directed, rule-based operations and sequencing to compute correct outcomes, which fits the review's definition of problem-solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses using SPM8 with stereotactic normalization (MNI space) and presents coordinate-based activation results in tables and figures (I6, I7, I9). Data derive from BOLD fMRI (I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not group comparison-only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult controls, reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental paradigm is a mental rotation visuo-spatial task (Shepard–Metzler figures), which is a perceptual/spatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). The paper frames the task as visuo-spatial/mental rotation and does not involve planning, sequencing, or multi-step problem-solving processes meeting the review's I5 definition. Therefore it fails I5 and must be excluded.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, it does not test a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The paradigm is a perceptual prototype-distortion categorization/learning task (categorizing distorted dot patterns with feedback), which primarily probes perceptual decision-making and category learning rather than goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the provided definition). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study of healthy adults that uses a goal-directed Internet search task (meeting I5, I6, and I8), the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinate results in either Talairach or MNI space (I7) nor explicitly indicate that voxelwise coordinates are available in tables/figures/supplementary materials (I9). The meta-analysis requires stereotactic coordinate reporting for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the information supplied. If coordinate tables or figures with coordinates are present in the article supplement or figures not included here, the study could be reconsidered for inclusion.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise/cluster results presented in main text). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet I5. Full text is complete and the study is a task-based PET study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain, stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and rCBF results. This is an empirical, whole-brain PET study that includes healthy adult controls and reports task-related rCBF stereotactic coordinates. However, the experimental task is a nonverbal theory-of-mind (attribution of intentions) task and related physical-causality control tasks. The meta-analysis requires studies of problem solving as operationalized (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing, or rule-based operations across domains). The ToM/comic-strip task assesses social inference/mentalizing rather than domain-general problem solving per the provided I5 definition, so I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude because I5 is not satisfied.

This PET study examines problem-solving/abstract reasoning using two canonical problem-solving tasks (WCST and Raven's Progressive Matrices) in a cohort of 41 healthy adults. The imaging modality is PET rCBF (task-related rCBF analyses). Voxelwise results are presented and compared across tasks. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I9). This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s core inclusion requirements. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the tasks are reaction-time and simple subtraction/mental arithmetic, not explicitly framed as problem-solving per the review’s definition), I6 (no whole-brain, task-based group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (no task-related stereotactic coordinate results in healthy adults), I8 (does not report BOLD or task-evoked rCBF analyses), and I9 (not applicable because task-related voxelwise results in healthy adults are not reported). This is a task-based fMRI study of chess problem solving (deliberative checkmate problems) in healthy adult participants (GM/M and novices). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults reporting whole-brain group analyses and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results. This is a task-based PET study with whole-brain SPM and quantitative rCBF analyses in a mixed sample of hypertensive patients and age-matched controls. No domain-general problem-solving tasks (semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical) are used. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

The full text is a complete, empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. This study is an fMRI investigation of financial decision-making under risk, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal followed by the need to figure out a way to reach it). The study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task used is word-stem completion / covert word generation (lexical retrieval), which is not described as goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects in healthy adults — one-sample t-tests were performed on control participants) and I8 (reports BOLD and rCBF analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task) and I7 (stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases are not reported in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete for screening.

Although this study is a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation in healthy adults with whole-brain group-level analysis reported in MNI space (meeting I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is somatosensory categorization/discrimination (deciding whether a stimulus is low or high intensity) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., goal-directed reasoning involving planning, sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 and is excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). It examines resting-state/default mode network connectivity derived from several cognitive and emotion fMRI tasks (oddball, continuous performance, Go/NoGo, emotion), validating task-derived resting activity and estimating heritability in twins. While the study includes whole-brain seed-based analyses with group-level effects in healthy adults (I6), reports results in MNI standard space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI measures (I8), and provides voxelwise results/figures (I9), it does not involve a task whose primary aim is problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing to find solutions). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the problem-solving task requirement (I5) and does not report stereotactic coordinate results (I7/I9). Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (uses whole-brain voxelwise data across healthy adult subjects via cross-subject analyses) and I8 (task-based fMRI BOLD data). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task is a sentence vs. picture verification/judgment, not a defined problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a goal), I7 (no Talairach/MNI coordinates reported), and I9 (no voxelwise stereotactic coordinates/tables or figures provided). Full text appears complete. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 and I7/I9 are not satisfied, the paper must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of decision-making using a modified Iowa Gambling Task (IGT). It meets I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is decision-making/risk-taking and reinforcement learning (IGT), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a correct/novel solution within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical, or similar frameworks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet the required problem-solving task definition.

This study uses task-based fMRI (BOLD) to assess a continuous mental arithmetic task (add consecutive digits and detect sums of 10), which fits the review’s operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations requiring sequencing, working memory, and rule-based execution). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses including a healthy comparison group with within-group task effects and between-group contrasts. Results are reported with stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activated clusters. Coordinates and activation maps are presented in the text/figures and analyses used SPM (voxelwise thresholds reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical human data). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion; core article content is present.

Full text is complete. Exclusion decision rationale: This study does not investigate problem-solving tasks. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standard space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does NOT study a problem-solving task — tasks are passive viewing of faces and houses, not goal-directed problem solving). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5. No other exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using arithmetic problem-solving (subtraction) tasks; includes whole-brain analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) with BOLD fMRI results. Meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria met.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study employing a semantic event-sequencing task that requires planning and sequencing of actions (meets I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses including within-group (Control) task effects (meets I6). Data were normalized to MNI space and stereotactic coordinates are reported (meets I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8). Coordinate results and voxelwise analyses are presented in the main text/results (meets I9). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., results are not ROI-only and include healthy-group task effects).

This study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task) though it meets other criteria. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI data reported), and I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion ID not met: I5 — the task is described and framed by the authors as a working-memory digit-sorting task (central executive and maintenance processes), with high accuracy and brief, rule-based sorting; it lacks the defining elements of problem solving in the review (goal-directed solution generation, planning/sequencing of actions to arrive at a novel or complex solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all inclusion criteria. It is an empirical, task-based fMRI study combined with [18F]DOPA PET in 29 healthy adults using a two-step sequential decision task that requires prospective planning and sequencing of actions (model-based control) to achieve reward, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (fMRI) and provides stereotactic coordinates for task-related activations (e.g., MNI coordinates x=16,y=8,z=-8 and x=42,y=24,z=-14) and refers to tables/figures (Table S3, Fig. 2) with voxelwise results. BOLD signal analyses are reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (N=8) using a goal-directed, rule-based stochastic decision/learning task where subjects must discover and execute actions to move a disk to a target (i.e., mapping identification, planning/sequencing actions under probabilistic transition rules). The paper reports group-level SPM analyses (whole-brain), BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) with tables/figures of voxelwise results. All required elements are present (behavioral task meeting the problem-solving definition, whole-brain group analysis, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analysis). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria met (not ROI-only, not patient-only comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical data). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and is INCLUDED.

The study used a mathematical/arithmetic series task requiring participants to infer a rule and select the next number—an explicit problem-solving paradigm (I5). It is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=12) with group-level random-effects analyses (I6). Data were normalized to Talairach coordinates and stereotactic results/ROIs are reported (I7). The paper reports both BOLD and CBF (ASL) analyses and derives CMRO2 (I8). Whole-brain voxelwise activation/deactivation maps and coordinates are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to between-group or clinical comparisons, and this is empirical human data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study with group-level random-effects analyses reporting Talairach coordinates and BOLD results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The paradigm examines task-set switching, Stroop and reverse-Stroop interference, and conflict-monitoring/fine-tuning processes rather than a goal-directed problem requiring planning/sequencing of actions to reach a novel solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete and reports a task-based BOLD fMRI whole-brain study in healthy adults (Experiment 2). However, the experimental task is a number magnitude comparison/selection task (choose larger or smaller number based on a cue) that manipulates symbolic distance and cognitive effort. This does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5), which requires goal-directed planning/sequencing or critical thinking to arrive at a correct or novel solution. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (results reported in main text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied; full text is complete.

Exclusion decision because the study does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The CSDLT is a spatial navigation/memory learning paradigm assessing hippocampal vs caudate-based strategies; although it has a goal (retrieve objects) and requires learning/flexibility, it primarily probes spatial memory and habit vs stimulus-response learning rather than the types of critical thinking/planning/sequencing operations across domains targeted by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported).
