Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a domain-general problem-solving task as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adult subjects performing a cognitive task (including a speeded Wisconsin Card Sorting Test) that qualifies as a problem-solving paradigm (requires inferring changing sorting rules, evaluating feedback, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-conforming responses). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed at the group level (maps normalized to a standard template), ROI identification was based on thresholded task-effect maps, and stereotactic coordinates (Talairach space) of local maxima are reported (Table I / figure descriptions). BOLD responses (task-related activity) and group-level statistics are described. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a methodological fMRI study evaluating ICA-based feature generation for prediction (datasets: thermal pain discrimination and familiar vs. novel visual scenes). It does not investigate problem-solving processes as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based solution-finding). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses on healthy adult participants are present) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the tasks are stimulus classification/recognition and pain discrimination, not problem-solving), I7 (the provided full text does not report stereotactic activation coordinates in Talairach/MNI space in the main text; while supplementary material is referenced, coordinates are not clearly presented in the supplied full text), I9 (no explicit tables/figures of coordinates in the provided text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the core task-related problem-solving inclusion criterion (I5).

This study uses an implicit sequence learning (Serial Reaction Time) task probing striatal/motor learning, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., goal-directed problem solving requiring planning, sequencing actions to reach a solution within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule sets). Although the paper meets other methodological criteria (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI/Talairach, and BOLD fMRI results), it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD whole-brain analyses in standardized Talairach space. However, the experimental tasks are sensorimotor choice/response-selection paradigms (auditory-manual and visual-vocal 8AFC) designed to probe dual-task/central bottleneck processing, not problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed identification/planning to reach a previously unknown solution or higher-order critical thinking). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level healthy adults), I7 (reports results in standardized space/Talairach), I8 (BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results indicated). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. While the study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation with healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in Talairach space, it does not examine 'problem-solving' as defined by the review. The tasks are reading/naming and parity (odd/even) judgments—rapid perceptual/semantic decisions that do not require planning, sequencing, or generation of solutions to a novel goal-directed problem. Thus inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to failure to meet I5.

Although this is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental paradigm is a perceptual/executive dual-task (color and letter discrimination with training) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed reasoning/planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution). The manuscript does not present tasks requiring planning, multi-step problem formulation, or operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule sets to derive previously unknown solutions, so it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5.

This is an fMRI study of visuomotor adaptation/object identification using a viewing-window paradigm in healthy adults. It meets I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-based fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (paper indicates peak activation locations are reported in tables/figures), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, it does not meet I5: the task is a sensorimotor adaptation and object-identification task rather than a domain-general problem-solving task as defined (involving goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations under semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rules to arrive at a solution). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to satisfy I5.

This PET study of the PASAT meets the meta-analysis criteria: PASAT requires rule-based arithmetic operations (adding two most recent digits), meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. The study used task-based PET measuring regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) with whole-brain SPM analyses at the group level in healthy adult participants (n=11). Results are reported with stereotactic Talairach coordinates and corrected voxelwise statistics; coordinate tables/figures are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of whole-brain task-related activation coordinates. Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adults that reports BOLD effects and localizes activations in Talairach space. It therefore meets I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic localization in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reporting acceptable). However, the experimental task is a perceptual judgment of line orientation (Benton’s JLO), a visuospatial orientation discrimination task, and does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5) involving goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at solutions. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. The experimental tasks are perceptual discrimination/comparison tasks (nonsymbolic number comparisons, spatial orientation, color judgments) that require magnitude or perceptual judgments rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or execution of operations to reach a previously unknown solution. The article does meet other methodological inclusion criteria: it reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), provides stereotactic MNI coordinates (I7), and reports BOLD-based analyses (I8); voxelwise results are available in the text/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I5.

This study reports task-based fMRI and PET imaging of Tower of London performance (a planning/problem-solving task meeting the review's problem-solving definition). It includes group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants, reports BOLD and rCBF results, and presents stereotactic-coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) via statistical parametric maps and coordinate reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses a task (WCST) that requires subjects to identify the correct sorting rule/dimension (goal-directed behavior) and to discover and apply that rule by trial-and-error or instruction, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (evaluate the problem, plan/sequence actions, execute rule-based operations to arrive at a correct solution). It is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=7) reporting group-level whole-brain event-related BOLD results. Stereotactic Talairach coordinates are provided and voxelwise activation is shown in figures/tables, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not a between-group-only or clinical comparison; not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, references).

This study is excluded because it does not address a problem-solving task (I5 not met): the tasks were bilateral finger tapping, passive listening, and visual checkerboard, which are sensory/motor/visual paradigms rather than problem-solving. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not problem-solving), I6 (no group-level whole-brain effects; authors state “No averaging across subjects” and present individual subject examples), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not reported in the full text). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses arithmetic equations (simple vs complex) requiring evaluation and execution of operations under rule sets—an algebraic/problem-solving task—thus meeting the definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain random-effects analyses at the group level in healthy adults (n=17) (I6), BOLD fMRI results (I8), and reports stereotactic peak coordinates/ROIs in standardized space (Talairach) (I7). Reporting of voxelwise/ROI coordinate results appears in text/tables, satisfying allowable reporting formats (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical).

The study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experimental task is a simple number-estimation/perceptual decision (judge whether number of dots is higher/lower than a figure) and does not involve goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning/sequencing of actions, or critical-thinking operations as required by I5. However, the study does meet other inclusion criteria: it reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and presents voxelwise results in text/figures/ROIs (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not a patient-group-only comparison, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded for failing I5 (problem-solving task).

Excluded because the study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met) and the imaging analysis is restricted to a prefrontal region-of-interest rather than a whole-brain voxelwise analysis (violates exclusion E3). The paper uses a dual-task/divided-attention paradigm (not framed as planning, sequencing, or rule-based problem solving) and focuses its second-level analyses after masking to Brodmann areas 44/45/46. It does, however, report stereotactic peak coordinates (Talairach) and PET rCBF activation results, so I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded: primary exclusion E3 (ROI-only results); inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9; inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that required rule-based task selection and sequencing to achieve a goal (minimize task difficulty), satisfying the meta-analytic definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-based operations). The study reports whole-brain group-level analyses (searchlight decoding and univariate analyses) in healthy adults, reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI), and uses BOLD fMRI. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (the Masterbrain logical deduction/search task) in healthy adults, meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. It includes group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses across 16 healthy participants; BOLD (fMRI) analyses; results reported with voxelwise thresholds and stereotactic coordinates normalized to MNI space presented in tables and figures. The manuscript contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full article content present). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (BOLD) reporting group-level MNI coordinates, but the experimental task is pairwise magnitude/timeline comparison (choose larger number or later event). That judgment/comparison task does not meet the review’s defined problem-solving construct (I5), which requires goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing actions or executing operations to reach a solution beyond a simple comparison judgment. All other inclusion criteria are satisfied (I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes a clear problem-solving task (the rule-finding task requires forming hypotheses, evaluating feedback, and discovering an unknown arithmetic rule), satisfying I5. Participants were healthy adult volunteers and group-level whole-brain analyses were reported (preprocessing, GLM, group subtraction analyses), satisfying I6. Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates, with Talairach conversions) satisfying I7. The study reports BOLD (fMRI) analyses throughout satisfying I8. Voxelwise/whole-brain subtraction and PPI results are reported and described in the main text and figures, satisfying I9. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a methodological fMRI signal-processing paper (EMCD) applying the method to resting-state, task-based (auditory), and naturalistic movie-watching data in healthy adults. It does not investigate a problem-solving task or problem-solving processes (no goal-directed problem solving, planning, rule-based solution, or critical thinking paradigms). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study problem-solving tasks), I6 (does not present a whole-brain, group-level task effect for a problem-solving paradigm), I7 (does not report stereotactic activation coordinates in Talairach/MNI space for problem-solving contrasts). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore excluded.

The PASAT is an algebraic/arithmetic, rule-based task that requires goal-directed operations (add last two digits), fitting the review's problem-solving definition (I5). The study includes healthy adult controls and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses for controls (one-sample t-test), satisfying I6. Results are reported in Talairach coordinates and BA labels (I7), and the study uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise/whole-brain activation results are presented in the main text/tables/figures (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This article is a methods/review paper describing a single-scan dynamic molecular imaging PET technique and summarizing prior task-based PET findings. It is not an original empirical PET/fMRI study that examines problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations within a rule set). It does not report whole-brain, group-level stereotactic coordinate results for a problem-solving task in healthy adults, nor does it report BOLD or rCBF analyses. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review without original human problem-solving data). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults specific to problem-solving), I7 (stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD/rCBF analysis). No inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study is an fMRI investigation of neural responses to advantageous and disadvantageous inequity using a perceptual discrimination and reward-feedback task. It meets I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports peak coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is a perceptual judgment with monetary feedback and social comparison, not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning, sequencing, or executing operations to arrive at a solution as defined by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

This study uses a working memory (externally ordered monitoring) task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to arrive at a solution). Although it includes healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain BOLD fMRI group effects with MNI normalization and voxelwise figures, it does not present a task that meets the review's definition of problem solving (I5 not met). Stereotactic coordinates for activation peaks are not explicitly reported in the provided text (I7 not met). Therefore it fails necessary inclusion criterion I5 (and I7) and is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) in healthy adults that reports whole-brain BOLD activations and figures in Talairach space. However, it does not meet the review's definition of a problem‑solving task (I5): the IGT is a decision‑making/reward‑learning task rather than a goal‑directed problem‑solving task involving explicit planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct solution. Also, while the paper states data were transformed to Talairach space and shows whole‑brain maps, it does not provide stereotactic coordinate tables of task‑related increases in the provided full text (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole‑brain analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/maps). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because I5 and I7 are not satisfied.

This study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. (a) Exclusion IDs met: None of the specified exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: None. Although participants are healthy adults, the paper does not present task-based whole-brain neuroimaging results. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (the task is a task-switching spatial-judgment paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level fMRI/PET analysis is reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates are reported), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF imaging analyses are reported). The authors explicitly state “We do not report the brain-imaging data in this paper, but focus on the behavioral data.” Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The tasks are bilateral finger tapping (motor) and digit–symbol substitution (DSST), neither of which clearly meet the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning, sequencing, and rule-based solution generation). The paper does include healthy adult participants, whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses, and BOLD fMRI measures, but the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables/coordinates for task-related increases in Talairach/MNI space in the excerpt. Therefore: inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task), I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting), and I9 (no clear voxelwise coordinate tables/figures in the provided text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates reported, and BOLD analyses, the task (Multi-Source Interference Task) is an interference/response-selection paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing operations within a rule set to arrive at a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI investigation that includes healthy control subjects and reports stereotactic coordinates, satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the cognitive task used is a working memory two-back task focused on maintenance/monitoring, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem identification, planning/sequencing, and rule-based solution generation). Therefore it does not meet I5. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion rationale: This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (study does not provide a healthy-group-only whole-brain task effect and primarily reports between-group contrasts comparing insomnia patients to controls). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task is verbal fluency, which does not clearly meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a correct/novel solution), I6 (no whole-brain group-level task analysis reported for healthy adults alone — main task effects are reported across mixed patients+controls or as between-group contrasts). Full text completeness: Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I5: its tasks are affective judgment and decision-making (emotional picture judgment and correlation with Iowa Gambling Task) rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing under formal rule sets such as semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses a counting Stroop interference task (an attentional/interference resolution paradigm), not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (which requires goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a novel solution). It does satisfy other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports results in Talairach space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete and methodological details (methods, results, discussion) are provided (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper is excluded only because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD analyses and stereotactic (MNI) results, the experimental tasks (Flanker, False Belief, attention/working memory, and Monetary Incentive Delay) do not constitute problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed operations requiring critical thinking/planning/sequencing to find solutions within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical, or similar rule frameworks). Hence inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a simple motor sequencing task in schizophrenia patients and matched controls, not a problem-solving task. It uses region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (caudate, anterior/posterior putamen+globus pallidus, thalamus) and reports percent-activated voxels within ROIs rather than whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears to contain core sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) and is treated as complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given these mismatches to the review objective and required reporting, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using the Tower of London task, which is a canonical problem-solving/planning task (goal-directed planning and sequencing). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with task effects across and within healthy groups, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space in tables/figures. Voxelwise results are reported and an ROI analysis was supplementary to whole-brain results. All inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. None of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet I5: the task is a spatial working-memory/encoding (chunking) and recall task rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed generation/planning of novel solutions or execution of rule-based problem solving). Although the study involves strategy use, it lacks the required problem-solving processes (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions to reach a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations).

This PET study used [11C]raclopride to measure dopamine release during a rewarded cued task-switching (executive control) paradigm. While the report includes stereotactic (MNI/ICBM) voxelwise peaks and accessible voxelwise results (I7 and I9 satisfied), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met): the paradigm is task-switching/response-speeding for reward rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning or novel solution generation. It also does not include whole-brain group-level analyses (analyses were restricted to striatal volumes/ROI and small-volume correction, so I6 not met). Finally, it is a molecular PET ligand study of D2 binding (ΔBPND) rather than a BOLD or rCBF activation study (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Thus the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of landmark/order judgments and script (activity) sequencing in familiar environments. It meets I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized space/MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results described). However, it does NOT meet I5: the tasks are order/match–mismatch judgments and memory retrieval of practiced landmark or action sequences, not problem-solving as defined (i.e., having a goal requiring participants to devise or plan a novel solution, evaluate/plan operations to reach the goal, or execute rule-based operations to find an unknown solution). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is an n-back working memory paradigm (updating/maintenance), which does not fit the review's defined problem-solving tasks (goal-directed planning/sequencing to derive novel solutions). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results registered/reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/cluster results available in figures/maps). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the n-back working memory task, with whole-brain group analyses (Randomise), reported stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analyses (satisfies I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task (n-back) is a working memory/update task and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed problem formulation, evaluating/planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults that reports BOLD whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates and group-level effects related to BDNF genotype. However, the experimental paradigms are virtual navigation and memory strategy tasks (4/8VM and CSDLT) aimed at dissociating hippocampus- versus caudate-dependent navigational strategies and memory-system recruitment. These tasks do not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5), which requires tasks designed around goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing under explicit rule sets (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical problem solving). Although navigation involves goal-directed behavior and sequencing, the study’s focus is spatial memory/strategy selection rather than domain-general or domain-specific problem solving as defined. Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (I5). The tasks used (auditory oddball, Sternberg item recognition, sensorimotor) are attention, working memory, and sensorimotor paradigms—not explicit problem-solving tasks involving goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution. Additionally, the paper does not report stereotactic coordinate tables (Talairach/MNI) of task-related increases (I7 not met). Included: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses are performed via ICA across subjects) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met. Therefore the paper fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (notably I5 and I7) and is excluded.

This study is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using motor imagery, motor observation, and motor execution tasks. It meets I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analyses), I7 (SPM normalization to standard space and reported activation results; coordinate tables indicated in supplementary materials), and I9 (voxelwise results available in supplementary materials). However, it does not meet I5: the tasks are motor imagery/observation/execution and BCI-control, not problem-solving tasks as defined (goal-directed critical thinking/planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical, or similar rule frameworks). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task requirement).

Excluded because analyses were restricted to an anatomical mask (visual association regions) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise analysis, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a 1-back visual category-matching / perceptual task, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis in healthy adults — analyses were constrained to a mask/ROI), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates in standard Talairach/MNI space reported). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task): the tasks are executive-control paradigms (counter-switching, stimulus-response compatibility, response inhibition) that probe attention-switching, interference resolution, and working memory updating, but do not require participants to formulate plans, sequence actions toward a novel goal, or generate solutions within a defined problem-solving framework. It does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI/Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failure to satisfy I5.

This is an fMRI study using a Go/No-Go response inhibition task to examine effects of acute alcohol on error monitoring/cognitive control. Inclusion: meets I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Exclusion: does NOT meet I5 — the task is response inhibition/error monitoring, not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning or sequencing to find a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates and voxelwise results. However, the cognitive tasks used are finger-tapping (motor) and a mental rotation task (visuospatial discrimination). Mental rotation is a perceptual/visuospatial transformation task and does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (goal-driven planning/sequencing/critical evaluation to derive a solution under a rule set). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analysis), I7 (Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results shown in figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., results are not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears complete. Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (I5) — the task used (BART) probes risk-taking/decision-making rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing to reach a correct solution. It also does not report stereotactic task-related activation coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (I7) and does not provide voxelwise coordinate results (I9). Satisfied inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain ROI-based analyses across healthy adult group; 22 healthy adults and group-level graph metrics) and I8 (reports BOLD and rCBF/CBF analyses). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were clearly triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task involves rule discovery/set-shifting consistent with problem-solving processes), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise PET analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I8 — the study does not report BOLD fMRI or regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) measures; it is a molecular PET study of D2 receptor binding potential (dopamine release) using [11C]FLB 457, not a hemodynamic BOLD/rCBF analysis. Exclusion criteria: none applicable (E3–E6 not met). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I8 required by the review protocol.

This is a methods paper using MEG–fMRI fusion with simulations and a single-subject visual checkerboard experiment, not a task-based problem-solving study. It does include BOLD/fMRI analyses but does not provide whole-brain, group-level task effects in healthy adults nor stereotactic coordinate tables. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analysis is ROI-based/single-ROI rather than whole-brain voxelwise reporting) and E5 (no healthy-group, group-level task effect — single-subject data only). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported). Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a cognitive task (silent random number generation) with whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses reporting stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results. Thus it meets I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the experimental task (random number generation) does NOT meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5: goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule-sets to reach a solution). No exclusion criteria are met (none of E3–E6 apply). Therefore the study is EXCLUDED because I5 is not satisfied.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task (IMT/DMT is an attention/working-memory/impulsivity task), so it fails inclusion I5. The analysis is restricted to a priori DLPFC region with Small Volume Correction (ROI-based), so it violates E3 (reports only ROI results) and does not provide whole-brain group-level healthy adult task effects (I6 not met; also E5 applies since no healthy-group task effect is reported). It does report BOLD analyses and stereotactic coordinates. Full text appears complete.

The study uses modafinil and an event-related fMRI cognitive control task (Preparing to Overcome Prepotency, POP) in healthy adults. While it meets criteria for whole-brain group fMRI analysis (I6), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and indicates stereotactic results are available in tables/supplementary (I7) and that voxelwise results are reported/available (I9), it does NOT study a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The POP task probes cognitive control/inhibitory processes rather than goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to arrive at novel solutions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The multi-source interference task (MSIT) used here is a response-conflict/attention/executive-control paradigm that requires identifying a target stimulus and resolving interference via a pre-specified rule, but it lacks the core problem-solving elements specified in I5 (e.g., deliberative planning, sequencing of actions to reach a novel solution or higher-order critical-thinking processes). Satisfied inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain effects in healthy adults present), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using the Tower of London (TOL) task, a well-established planning/problem-solving paradigm (meets problem-solving definition). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with thresholding corrected for multiple comparisons, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for activations, and presents voxelwise BOLD results in figures/tables. Participants were healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided and appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses, it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks are mental-rotation/spatial-transformation judgments (imagined self vs. object rotations assessing visibility of a textured cube) rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, or applying rule-based procedures to arrive at a novel or correct solution as defined in I5. Therefore I5 is not satisfied; all other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study was excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is a rule-switching/stimulus-response (SR) mapping paradigm examining cognitive control and effector modality (saccade vs. manual) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring participants to identify/plan novel solutions across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or other domains. It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise stereotactic results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task qualifies as problem-solving — Wisconsin Card Sorting Task requires identifying/implementing changing sorting rules, planning/sequence and set-shifting), I6 (whole-brain, data-driven functional network analysis with group-level effects reported both in healthy controls (Experiment 1) and in control group comparisons), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analysis reported). I9 is also satisfied insofar as voxelwise, whole-brain network results are presented in figures and AAL-based mappings. Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the paper does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI peak coordinates/tables) for task activations/contrasts. The analyses are presented as network maps, histograms, and AAL-region percentages but no standardized coordinate tables or peak coordinates are provided. Because I7 is required, the study must be excluded.

This study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. It investigates attribute set switching (task-set inertia/executive control), which is a rule-following switching task rather than a problem-solving task as defined (no novel goal-directed problem formulation, planning/sequencing to discover solutions). Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not satisfied. Although the study uses task-based whole-brain fMRI and reports stereotactic (MNI) normalisation and BOLD analyses (satisfying I7 and I8) and coordinates/results likely available in figures/tables (I9), the sample is a mixed adolescent–adult cohort and the reported group-level whole-brain analyses are across the combined sample (no clear whole-brain group analysis restricted to healthy adults only), so I6 is not clearly met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study does not meet the review's problem-solving task definition (I5). It uses task-switching/simple perceptual and response-mapping tasks (color, face, motion, spatial frequency) that do not require participants to identify/plan or generate novel solutions or perform higher-order problem-solving (evaluation, planning/sequencing actions to reach a goal). It instead investigates stimulus–response associations and executive control/competition. The full text is complete and the study does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (I6), stereotactic coordinates reported (I7), BOLD analyses (I8), and voxelwise results available (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclude due to failure to satisfy I5.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task used (affective Stroop / numerosity judgment under emotional distraction) probes attentional control and affective interference during a perceptual decision, not a problem-solving paradigm involving goal-driven planning/sequencing or executing operations within a semantic, algebraic, logical, or other rule-based framework to derive a (novel) solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI case study (single healthy 21-year-old male) that investigates planning/problem-solving using a virtual navigation roadblock task and a virtual Tower of London. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of problem-solving/planning), I7 (results referenced in Talairach stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). However, the study fails to meet I6: it does not include a group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults (n=1 single-subject case study). This violates exclusion criterion E5 (study does not include any healthy-group task effect). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting several other technical criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using Raven-style fluid intelligence problems (induction, visualization, spatial relationships) that require rule inference and goal-directed problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects group analyses, BOLD signal results, and stereotactic coordinates (with coordinates reported and discussed). Voxelwise results are presented in maps and supplementary materials. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I9). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a Trail-Making set-shifting task that meets the problem-solving definition (goal-directed sequencing/switching). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA) and BOLD results. However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the excerpt (although images/figures are referenced and Talairach normalization is described). Because inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) cannot be verified from the supplied full text, I must exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the provided content.

This study uses a working memory (auditory letter encoding/rehearsal and delay) task focused on phonologic loop processes, not a problem-solving paradigm as defined (no goal-directed problem decomposition, planning/sequencing of operations to find a novel solution). Although it reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI results in healthy adults with stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates and voxelwise analyses, it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reporting, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to failure to meet inclusion criterion I5.

This study uses the AX Continuous Performance Task (AXCPT), a cognitive control/context-processing task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a solution). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5. Additionally, the sample includes adolescents (age range 12–25), so it does not clearly meet the requirement of healthy adult participants for whole-brain group-level effects (I6 not met). The study does include task-based BOLD fMRI (I8) and reports voxelwise/whole-brain results and ROI coordinates in standardized space allowing reporting of results (I9; ROI coordinates provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task not problem-solving), I6 (healthy adult group not clearly satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: none.

This study uses the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., requiring identification/planning/sequencing to reach a correct or novel solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is NOT met. The full text is complete and the study does meet multiple methodological criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses across healthy young participants), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the article must be excluded because it fails I5.

This fMRI study uses a rule-switching task that requires participants to identify and apply task rules to reach correct responses (goal-directed, rule-based operations in bivalent/univalent trials), which meets the review's operational definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adult participants (n=20), with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., 24 20 18) reported and FWE-corrected results; voxelwise results are described in text and figures. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study uses a complex working memory (reading/listening span) task rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined in the protocol. While it includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and reports voxelwise results, it does not examine problem solving (planning/sequencing/deriving novel solutions) across domains. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that examines arithmetic problem-solving (multiplication verification), using a within-subject design with pre/post intervention. It reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses of BOLD activity, uses stereotactic space (Talairach) for localization, and presents voxelwise activation results (cluster-level corrected maps and coordinates referenced via Talairach Client). The task involves evaluating presented solutions and applying arithmetic rules to decide correctness, which fits the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content appears complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports ROI-restricted analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a simple auditory-motor tapping task, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adults; analyses were restricted to a priori ROIs and matched triplet MANOVAs), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates of task-related increases are reported), I9 (voxelwise whole-brain results or coordinates are not provided in text/tables). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the review objective and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of sunk-cost decision-making (continuing vs. not continuing an investment). It meets inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain, group-level one-sample t-tests reported) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). However it does not meet the core problem-solving definition (I5): the task is an economic decision-making/risk task rather than a problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to arrive at a correct solution. The provided full text also does not present stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) in the supplied content, so I7 is not satisfied; voxelwise coordinate tables/coordinates in figures or supplements are not available in the supplied text, so I9 is also not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded.

Although this fMRI study includes a number-addition task that qualifies as a problem-solving paradigm (meets I5), uses whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults (meets I6), and reports BOLD-based results (meets I8) with voxelwise activation shown in Talairach-space figures (meets I9), the provided full text does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) as numeric coordinate results or tables. Inclusion criterion I7 explicitly requires stereotactic coordinate reporting, which is not present in the supplied article content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I exclude this study because it fails to meet I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting).

This is a whole-brain fMRI BOLD study in healthy adults with voxelwise analyses (meets I6 and I8). However, the task is a motor mental-rotation/sensorimotor transformation task and does not match the review's specified definition of a problem-solving task that requires goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing of actions to find a (novel) solution (I5 not met). Additionally, the full text does not report stereotactic activation coordinates (Talairach/MNI) or coordinate tables/figures for task-related peaks, so it fails I7 (and the acceptable voxelwise-coordinate provision I9 is not satisfied). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I5 and I7/I9).

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task (sentence–picture matching with feedback to bias spatial frame-of-reference interpretations) does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task. The task lacks a clear goal requiring participants to devise or plan actions or perform critical-thinking processes to generate a previously unknown solution (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study uses a simple event-related finger-tapping task (visual checkerboard + bilateral tapping) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/solution evaluation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults present for the control group), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results/maps reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Excluded because the task is motor/visual, not problem-solving (I5 not met).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15) using a relational matching task that requires subjects to evaluate and integrate relations according to explicit rules to produce correct responses—meeting the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed evaluation and rule-based operations). The study reports group-level whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses (Dimension > Feature contrasts), provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activated clusters (e.g., left RLPFC at −36 57 9), and applies appropriate statistical correction. All required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this paper is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and BOLD results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), the task is an n-back working memory paradigm. The meta-analysis defines problem-solving tasks as requiring goal-directed identification/planning and execution to arrive at a (sometimes novel) solution. The n-back primarily probes working memory/maintenance and updating rather than problem-solving/planning or critical-evaluative processes as defined in I5. Therefore I5 is not met and the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a goal-directed virtual maze requiring subjects to plan and sequence actions to find a hidden goal, meeting the review's definition of problem-solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy control task effects (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., 18 -61 40) (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Coordinate results and activation maps are reported in the full text (I9). It is not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical human fMRI data, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used a prolonged visual search task (perceptual/attention/fatigue paradigm) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (no goal-directed problem-solving, planning, or rule-based solution processes were assessed). The full text contains whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults and reports BOLD results (satisfying I6 and I8). The manuscript refers to activation tables/figures, so voxelwise results are indicated as available (I9). However, stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space are not clearly reported in the provided full text (I7 not confirmed). Therefore the key inclusion criterion I5 is not met, leading to exclusion. Full text appears complete.

This study used the Stroop task (cognitive inhibition/conflict) rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined in I5 (no planning/sequencing or rule-based solution generation). Analysis was conducted within predefined ROIs (WFU_PickAtlas) rather than an unconstrained whole-brain voxelwise analysis, triggering exclusion criterion E3. The paper does report stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, so I7 and I8 are satisfied, but I5 and I6 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The Hayling sentence completion test is a verbal initiation/fluency and executive control task probing semantic completion and response initiation/inhibition, but it does not clearly embody the review’s specified problem-solving construct (a goal-driven requirement to evaluate, plan/sequence actions and execute operations within a rule set to reach a previously unknown solution). The paper does meet other technical criteria: it reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult participants (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), and presents voxelwise results in the text/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only, nor non-empirical). Therefore it must be excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I5.

The study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by I5. It uses a pure attentional set-switching/motor-response switching task (switching between horizontal and vertical spatial dimensions) rather than a task requiring goal-directed problem-solving, planning/sequencing of actions to reach a solution, or executing operations within a semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule set to derive a novel or correct solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails I5.

This study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by inclusion criterion I5. The Kana Pick-out Test (KPT) is a dual-task assessing divided attention, working memory, reading and vowel detection, not a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing or applying rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task), I7 (the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space), and I9 (no coordinates/tables/figures with stereotactic results are present in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text provided is incomplete (only a browser redirect/metadata). Cannot verify whether the study uses a problem-solving task (I5), includes healthy adult group whole-brain analyses (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates (I7), or reports BOLD/rCBF analyses (I8). Title suggests disease groups (carotid stenosis and white matter disease), so it likely does not focus on healthy adults, but this cannot be confirmed from the incomplete content. Therefore I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met (or unverifiable): I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Full text incomplete and insufficient to assess eligibility.

This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is a cued task-switching semantic categorization paradigm (manmade/natural; large/small) assessing executive control, cue processing, and semantic retrieval, but it does not involve goal-directed problem solving as defined (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions to arrive at a novel or correct solution). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results and coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria were violated (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I5.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and group-level effects, the task (multisource interference task, MSIT) is a response-conflict/cognitive control task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The MSIT requires conflict monitoring and rapid button-mapping responses rather than goal-directed problem solving that involves evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions, and deriving a previously unknown solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task as defined) is not met. Other inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses a two-choice prediction decision-making task in a sample including methamphetamine-dependent patients and matched controls. Although it includes whole-brain group-level fMRI (BOLD) analyses in healthy adult controls reported in Talairach space (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is a decision-making/prediction paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion criterion I5.

This study does not address problem-solving as defined in the review (I5 not met): the task is an attentional/emotional CPT-END paradigm, not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution. It also does not present a within-healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I6 not met) — analyses focus on between-group contrasts (patients vs. each other and vs. HC) and an across-groups emotional vs. cognitive map, so no healthy-only group-level task activation is reported. The study does report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and whole-brain BOLD fMRI results and presents voxelwise results in tables/figures, satisfying I7, I8, and I9. Because the paper effectively only provides between-group contrasts / lacks a healthy-group task effect, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Summary of criteria: Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the task does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the paradigms used (prospective memory / attention coordination task with target detection and ongoing judgments) do not constitute a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a novel solution). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI-normalized stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI investigation (BOLD) that reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and includes healthy adult participants and group-level analyses; however, the experimental task is a probabilistic reversal learning paradigm focused on reinforcement learning and cognitive flexibility, not a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (i.e., tasks requiring goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks to derive a solution). Therefore it fails to meet I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5.

This is an fMRI pharmacological study of acute hydrocortisone effects using an n-back working memory task. It does not examine problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed generation/planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution). Inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only report, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it does not address the required problem-solving task (I5 not met).

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. It uses the Eriksen flanker task to study error recognition, reconcentration, and post-error adjustment (conflict monitoring/response selection), which does not involve setting a goal and devising/planning a novel sequence of operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based study of problem solving). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore EXCLUDED for the meta-analysis because it fails I5.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, task-based BOLD analyses of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, which requires rule discovery, set maintenance and set-shifting—processes consistent with problem solving (goal-directed identification/planning/execution under rule constraints). Group-level whole-brain results are reported for matched healthy adult controls (mean age 54) with stereotactic normalization (Talairach space) and coordinate tables/peaks reported. BOLD contrasts and between- and within-group task effects for the healthy group are presented. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (i.e., core article content), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a methodological reproducibility investigation using finger flexion (motor) and 2-back (working memory) tasks to compute minimum detectable change (MDC) of fMRI metrics in healthy adults. It does not study problem-solving as defined (goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). The analyses focus on ROI-based measures (PSM and DLPFC) for MDC calculations rather than reporting task-related whole-brain stereotactic activation coordinates for problem-solving contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion E3 (reports only ROI results / primary analyses are ROI-based). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level fMRI maps were generated across sessions) and I8 (reports BOLD/percent signal change). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task) and I7 (does not report task-related stereotactic coordinate results relevant to problem-solving). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using BOLD and ASL (meets I6 and I8). However, the experimental paradigm is a modified Stroop (inhibition/switching), which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Additionally, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates for task-related activations in the excerpt provided (I7 not met). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Included criteria met: I6, I8. Included criteria not met: I5, I7 (I9 not applicable because I7 is not satisfied).

This paper is a methodological/tutorial article on anatomical ROI-based fMRI classification, not an empirical whole-brain, task-based fMRI/PET study of problem-solving. It focuses on ROI methods and presents an example classification of auditory stimuli using ROI masks rather than whole-brain voxelwise analyses; no stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or whole-brain group-level activation tables are reported. Although it reports BOLD fMRI data in healthy adults for an example (so I8 is met), it does not study a problem-solving task (I5 not met), does not include whole-brain group-level analyses (I6 not met), and does not report stereotactic coordinates (I7 not met). It therefore violates exclusion E3 (reports only ROI results). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the review definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experimental task is a probabilistic category/classification (weather-prediction) learning paradigm focused on declarative vs. nondeclarative memory systems and procedural/category learning, not on goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing actions, or applying explicit semantic/algebraic/logical rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. The full text does meet multiple other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7), BOLD/fMRI analyses (I8), and provision of voxelwise results in figures/coordinates (I9). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because it fails I5 (task definition).

The task used (letter-matching by name or physical identity) is a simple perceptual/rule-matching task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and execution to arrive at a novel or complex solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The study does meet other methodological criteria: it includes whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and allows voxelwise results presented in text/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The wayfinding task meets the review's problem-solving definition and the study includes healthy adult participants, whole-brain fMRI analyses, and BOLD results. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the excerpt supplied, which is required by inclusion criterion I7. Therefore the study cannot be included based on the provided information.

Full text is complete. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 — the task is a dynamic decision-making/reward-selection paradigm (impulsivity/self-control) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar rule frameworks). Therefore the study does not meet the core problem-solving task criterion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Given that ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 is not satisfied, exclude.

This PET study used [11C]-raclopride binding during a probabilistic classification (weather prediction) task in healthy adults. It does not meet the review’s requirements: it reports only ROI-based PET binding analyses rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results, and therefore violates exclusion E3. It also fails multiple inclusion criteria: I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate tables/voxelwise coordinates reported), and I8 (does not report BOLD or rCBF measures — it reports neurotransmitter binding PET). Additionally, the task is a probabilistic classification/learning paradigm (incidental feedback-based learning), which is not clearly a problem-solving task as defined by I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports an event-related, task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adult participants (n=11) performing the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (WCST). The WCST requires a goal-directed process (determine matching rule and adjust behavior to reach correct matches), involving problem-solving subprocesses (evaluating feedback, planning set-shifts, executing rule-based actions). The paper presents group-level random-effects whole-brain BOLD analyses, stereotactic normalization into Talairach space, and tables/figures of activation peaks (voxelwise results). Thus it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This article is largely a narrative summary/review of multiple structural and functional neuroimaging studies from the authors' laboratory rather than a single primary empirical report providing whole-brain stereotactic coordinate tables. Although it describes task-based PET and fMRI experiments using mental-arithmetic (MIST) in healthy adults (meeting I5, I6 and I8), the full text as provided does not report task-related activation coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (I7 not met) nor clearly provide voxelwise coordinate tables/figures or indicate their availability (I9 not met). Because the manuscript functions as a non-empirical review/synthesis rather than presenting original, coordinate-based whole-brain results suitable for meta-analysis, it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical review without original coordinate data). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that includes healthy control participants and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and BOLD signal analyses (satisfies I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental paradigm is an externally-ordered working memory task (monitoring items and recognition), which taps working memory/monitoring processes rather than a problem-solving task as defined for this review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations within a rule set to derive a novel solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it fails I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the review definition) while meeting I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study investigates theory of mind (mentalizing) using an imaginative story-generation PET task, not a problem-solving paradigm. It does not require subjects to define a goal and then identify/plan and execute rule-based operations to reach a solution, so inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain PET with group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates), I8 (reports rCBF analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures).
