No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not address the review’s required problem-solving task.

The study uses a working memory (listening/reading span) task rather than a problem-solving task as defined for this review (no goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel/correct solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The full text is complete and the study meets technical/methodological criteria: I6 (includes whole-brain group-level analyses with healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results), and I9 (voxelwise results are reported/available). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task (I5 not met).

This study does not meet the meta-analysis’ definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task used is a Stroop interference paradigm assessing response inhibition/selective attention/conflict resolution, which does not involve goal-directed problem solving as defined (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions, and executing operations within a rule set to reach a correct/novel solution). The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including analyses in the healthy/non-demented group), I7 (results reported in Talairach stereotactic space/tables), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the provided definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using the Wisconsin Word Sorting Task, which requires discovering and applying classification rules by trial-and-error (goal-directed rule discovery, planning, set-shifting and execution), meeting the review's definition of problem-solving. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects), with stereotactic normalization into MNI/Talairach space and thresholded statistical maps, and BOLD fMRI data. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion describing coordinate-based activation peaks. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not examine problem-solving tasks as defined in the review (I5 not met). It investigates resting-state and block-based visual/auditory paradigms (emotional videos, stories) to characterize functional connectome patterns, not goal-directed problem-solving, planning, or rule-based solution operations. The article does include group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy participants and reports BOLD/task-related activation detection (satisfies I6 and I8). However, stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates for task activations are not presented in the provided full text (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet the core inclusion criterion I5 (and also I7).

This is a methodological paper proposing a clustering/regression-mixture approach for fMRI analysis, applied to auditory and motor tasks. It does not study a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). Although it analyzes BOLD fMRI data (I8) and presents voxelwise activation maps/figures (I9), it does not perform or report a whole-brain, group-level analysis of problem solving in healthy adults (I6 not met) nor report stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases in MNI/Talairach space (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study should be excluded from the problem-solving meta-analysis.

Although this is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, the experimental tasks (delayed match to sample and delayed nonmatch to sample) are memory/recognition and inhibition paradigms rather than problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing, critical evaluation, or operations to arrive at novel solutions). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The full text is complete and provides methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are triggered (the paper does not report only ROIs, is empirical, and includes within-group task effects). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an fMRI study of occupational choice/decision-making (conflict without objective correct answer). It includes healthy adult participants, whole-brain group analyses, reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) and BOLD/PPI results. However, the task (occupational choice) is a preference/decision/conflict task lacking the core elements of problem solving as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a correct or novel solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates. However, it does not investigate a problem-solving task per the review definition (goal-directed planning, evaluation, sequencing or executing operations to reach a solution). The experimental tasks are social-language judgments (situational appropriateness vs. literal correctness) assessing irony/metaphor comprehension and theory-of-mind processes, not problem-solving across domains. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, while I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This study investigates theory-of-mind (belief attribution) in schizophrenia using fMRI. Although it includes healthy adult group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses reported in MNI coordinates (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the experimental task (Belief Attribution Task) is a social cognition/theory-of-mind paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no explicit goal-directed problem formulation, planning/sequencing of actions, or execution of rule-based operations to reach a solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task as defined in I5. The task probes conflict, task-switching, and error monitoring using species identification and implicit reward-based switches, which assess cognitive control and outcome prediction rather than goal-directed problem solving (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks to arrive at a solution). The full text is complete and the study meets I6–I9 (whole-brain group fMRI analyses in healthy adults; reports MNI coordinates; BOLD/fMRI analyses reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Thus excluded due to failure to satisfy I5.

The study does not meet the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task (forethought/congruency judgment of pictured sequences) measures expectation/anticipation and detection of incongruency rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires generating/implementing sequences of actions or operations to reach a solution. It does, however, meet several other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, task-based fMRI with group-level effects in healthy adult controls (I6); stereotactic (MNI) coordinate reporting (I7); and BOLD/fMRI analyses (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This study investigates perceptual decision-making (detection of an animal among distractors) and how motivation shifts response bias, using event-related fMRI. It does not examine problem solving as defined by the review (goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions or critical thinking processes to arrive at a correct/new solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The study does meet other methodological criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6); reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7); reports BOLD analyses (I8); and voxelwise results are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it fails I5 (does not study problem-solving).

This is an fMRI study of number notation usage using number comparison and digit identification tasks in healthy adult binumerates. While it meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group-level fMRI BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates reported), it does not examine 'problem-solving' as defined by the review (goal-driven tasks requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The tasks are magnitude comparison and digit identification (perceptual/semantic/automaticity judgments) rather than problem-solving/critical-thinking tasks. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not satisfied. Met inclusion criteria: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

While this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental paradigm (guessing color/suit of playing cards) does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The correct response on each trial is determined entirely by chance and there is no requirement to identify or execute a strategy to reach a goal-defined solution space; authors explicitly state there is no possibility of associative learning and that outcomes are chance-determined. Although subjects reported using strategies and working memory was engaged, the task lacks the core elements of problem solving as defined (goal-directed planning/sequence of rule-based operations to reach a correct/novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of imagined egocentric spatial transformations (hand vs. viewer rotation). While it reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in standardized MNI space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental tasks are mental rotation/perspective-taking and left/right handedness judgments rather than goal-directed problem solving as defined by the review (no explicit goal requiring planning/sequencing of operations to reach a solution or application of a rule-based problem-solving framework). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task as defined) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review objective of examining problem-solving tasks. Specifically: it does not involve a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met)—the task is perceptual judgment of impossible vs possible figures rather than goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based solution operations. Also, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (I7 not met) in the excerpt (coordinates may be in omitted tables/figures, but not present here). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded.

This is an fMRI study of hypothesis testing/category induction consistent with problem-solving processes (meets I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adult participants (meets I6) and uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8). However, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for reported activations in the excerpt (only Brodmann areas and cluster descriptions are given), so inclusion criterion I7 is not satisfied. I9 (allowing coordinates in tables/figures/supplement) cannot be confirmed from the provided text. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not met/confirmable from the provided content, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD coordinate results. However, the experimental paradigm is an object working memory (maintenance and recognition/match-to-sample) task with financial incentives. It does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5): there is no evidence of goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations to derive previously unknown solutions or engage critical thinking/planning processes as defined. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. The full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (n=7) using a visuomotor ‘2 × 10’ sequence-learning paradigm that requires subjects to discover and plan a correct sequence of actions by trial-and-error (goal-directed sequencing and rule-based action selection), which fits the review’s operational definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain echo-planar BOLD fMRI analyses, identifies learning-related activation foci across subjects, performs group-level comparisons (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across subjects), and provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates (Table 1). BOLD signal (ΔSI) and activated-pixel analyses are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, and discussion).

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study (go/no-go inhibitory control) in boys aged 8–20 including ADHD patients, unaffected siblings, and matched controls. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is inhibitory control/go–no-go, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (participants are children and adolescents, not healthy adults). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study does not address the review objective (problem-solving in healthy adults) and must be excluded.

This is a methods paper presenting a region-growing algorithm for fMRI data analysis and demonstrating it on simulated data and an auditory task dataset. It does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). It does not report whole-brain group-level task effects in healthy adult participants (I6 not met) and does not present stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI space (I7 not met). It does report BOLD fMRI analyses (I8 met). Therefore it fails to meet several required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criterion E5 (it does not include any healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7 (also I9 not applicable). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (no healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It examines implicit rule/sequence learning in a serial reaction time task (procedural/anticipation and memory retrieval), not goal-directed problem solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing to reach an unknown solution as defined by the meta-analysis. It does include whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6) and reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) or explicit voxelwise coordinate tables/figures in the text supplied, so I7 is not satisfied from the available content; I9 (acceptability of coordinates in figures/tables) is also not demonstrably met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the provided information. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses task-based BOLD fMRI (Hayling Sentence Completion) which engages executive/semantic processes (evaluating sentence context and generating an appropriate response), consistent with the review’s definition of problem-solving within a semantic framework (I5). It reports whole-brain, random-effects SPM analyses with group-level effects including a healthy adult control group (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for task-related activations (I7), and reports BOLD fMRI results (I8). Voxelwise/cluster results are described in text and figures allowing coordinate extraction (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), healthy-group task effects are reported, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task-switching (intrinsically cued letter-classification with stimulus–response mappings) rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined in the review (I5). Although the task requires rule-based responses, it does not require participants to formulate plans, evaluate problems, or generate previously unknown solutions; it is an executive control/task-switching task rather than a problem-solving task. The full text is complete and shows whole-brain group analyses using fMRI BOLD, stereotactic labeling, and reported results. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is NOT met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic/MNI/Talairach reporting and labeling), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

While this is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results in MNI coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is a magnitude-comparison/number-mining comparison task (select larger magnitude) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5. The task does not require goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or higher-order problem solving/critical thinking to arrive at a novel solution; it is a perceptual/numeric comparison judgment. Therefore I5 is not met and the study is excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a methodology paper on automatic ICA-based denoising of fMRI data. While the study uses task data (category learning) from healthy adult subjects and performs whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined for this review (goal-directed problem-solving/planning/executive rule-based solution). The tasks are category learning/dual-task paradigms rather than explicit problem-solving across domains. Furthermore, the full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables (Talairach/MNI) of task-related activation peaks required by I7. Therefore it fails to meet I5 and I7. No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered.

The study reports a task-based fMRI/EEG experiment in healthy adults (n=8) using a mental-arithmetic (continuous subtraction) task that involves goal-directed operations, sequencing, and rule-based computation consistent with problem-solving (I5). It includes whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM99 analyses with group-level one-sample t-tests across subjects (I6). BOLD (fMRI) analyses are reported (I8). Data were normalized to an MNI template and stereotactic coordinates are reported in the text (e.g., [−42, −10, 42]), with voxelwise results and thresholding described, satisfying the requirement for coordinate reporting (I7) and acceptable reporting formats (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only results, no between-group-only contrasts, not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study does not meet the review objective for two main reasons: (1) I5 not met — the task is a Go/NoGo response inhibition paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based solution discovery). (2) I6 not met — participants are ages 8–20 (predominantly minors/adolescents); the meta-analysis requires whole-brain group effects in healthy adult individuals. The study does meet other technical criteria: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/Talairach/MNI), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based on I5 and I6 not being satisfied.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (I6, I7, I8 satisfied), the behavioral paradigms (response-switching and visual-switching) examine task-set switching, response selection, and attentional control. Subjects are instructed which rules to apply and must switch between these instructed rules; they are not required to identify or discover solutions, to engage in open-ended problem formulation, or to perform goal-directed problem solving as defined in I5 (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Because the primary aim and tasks do not meet the review’s definition of problem-solving across domains, the study is excluded.

This study is a methods paper using real-time fMRI and SPRT, applied to face vs. house perception and simulations; it does not investigate problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (I5 not met). The empirical real-data example is a single-subject/ROI-focused FFA analysis rather than a whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults (I6 not met). The paper reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8 met). It appears analyses focus on an ROI (mask of 717 voxels) and comparisons within that ROI rather than whole-brain voxelwise, and results are presented as ROI maps rather than providing stereotactic coordinate tables for whole-brain group effects; thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Summary: Excluded because E3 applies; inclusion criteria met: I8; inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, I9.

The study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving per the review definition (I5). The task involves passive viewing of videos with button presses to indicate change points (event parsing/attention), not goal-directed problem solving requiring planning, sequencing, or rule-based operations to find solutions. The paper does meet other relevant inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/maps reported in figures). However, the manuscript does not present stereotactic coordinates in the provided full text, so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., ROI-only, between-group-only, non-empirical). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing key inclusion criteria (primarily I5; also I7 not satisfied based on provided text).

The study uses task-based fMRI (movie watching) but does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing rule-based solutions). It reports developmental (child vs adult) group comparisons and modularity analyses but does not report task-related activation foci in stereotactic coordinates for a problem-solving contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm) and I7 (no task-related stereotactic coordinate activation results reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (study presents group comparisons and does not provide healthy-group task effect/contrast relevant to problem-solving). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

This fMRI study in healthy adults examines sequencing of actions (script task) and sentence-word order, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI addressing sequencing/planning/problem-like processing), I6 (healthy adult participants with reported group-level whole-brain activation summaries), and I8 (BOLD fMRI results reported). However, the paper does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space or provide voxelwise coordinate tables/figures (only Brodmann areas and ROI-based subject counts), so it fails I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) clearly apply; the study is not an ROI-only analysis in the methodological sense but lacks standardized coordinates. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to missing I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results/tables/figures available). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5. The experimental task is a probability-learning and decision-making paradigm (learning color–payoff associations and choosing gambles). While it involves inference and maximizing reward, it does not constitute a problem-solving task as defined for the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a novel or correct solution across domains). Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis’ core inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text is a whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI study of associative visuomotor learning (trial-and-error mapping of visual patterns to finger movements). It meets inclusion criteria I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (coordinates reported in text/figures). However, it does not meet I5: the experimental task is visuomotor associative learning rather than a problem-solving task defined as goal-directed critical thinking/planning/sequencing within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar frameworks to reach a previously unknown solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

Full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects reported for healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (task-related rCBF PET analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise results available in main text/tables/figures). Failed inclusion criterion I5: the experimental task is a modified word-stem completion designed to evoke emotional ambivalence and evaluative judgment (good/bad/neither) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring planning/sequencing actions or executing operations within a rule set to reach a solution. The task assesses emotional conflict resolution and evaluative processing, not the defined problem-solving processes required by the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5.

This study does not meet the review’s problem-solving task requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level task-based fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a Flanker selective attention/inhibition task, not a problem-solving task as defined—no goal-directed planning/sequencing to derive a novel solution), I7 (stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases are not presented in the provided full text; cluster activations are described but coordinates/tables are not shown). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only analyses, not a non-empirical paper, contains within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion; tables/figures with coordinates are not included in the provided content. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the specific problem-solving task requirement (I5) and does not provide explicit stereotactic coordinate listings in the provided text (I7).

This is a methodological fMRI study of prospective motion correction using a foot-movement (right-leg lift) paradigm. It does not study a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning, sequencing or rule-based solution processes). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adult volunteers) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). I7 (stereotactic coordinates) are not clearly reported in the provided full text excerpt. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the review’s core task domain (I5).

While this PET study reports whole-brain, group-level rCBF results in healthy adults with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and rCBF analyses (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in I5. The tasks are visual working memory and a conditional colour-response associative learning paradigm (memory/association and stimulus-response mapping), not higher-level problem solving involving goal-oriented planning, evaluation, sequencing, or generating previously unknown solutions. No exclusion criteria are otherwise met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

This is a methodological fMRI study of a sparse-regression deconvolution method (SPFM) validated on simulated data and a visuomotor single-trial finger-tapping task in five healthy subjects. It does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed cognitive problem solving, planning/sequencing, rule-based solution). Although it reports empirical fMRI BOLD results (I8 met), it does not evaluate problem-solving across domains (I5 not met). Additionally, the paper presents mostly single-subject/within-run analyses (no clear group-level whole-brain statistical contrasts reported to satisfy I6) and does not present stereotactic coordinate tables for task-related activations in standardized space (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that investigates learning and execution of rule-based tasks (task model assembly, goal-directed behavior). It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. The tasks require setting goals and applying/implementing rule sets to produce correct responses, matching the review definition of problem solving (rule-based evaluation, planning/sequencing, and execution). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a mental-arithmetic (serial subtraction) task (meets I5) and analyzes BOLD signals (meets I8). However, the paper is methodological (fMRI used to model/validate fNIRS regressors) and does not present a whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation analysis with stereotactic peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The manuscript reports optically weighted channel/forehead activation maps and signal-comparison metrics rather than standard group-level whole-brain SPM-style coordinates. Therefore it does not satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis) or I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

The study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (Inclusion I5). Although it is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the cognitive task used (multi-source interference task) probes attention/executive control/conflict resolution rather than goal-directed problem solving as defined in I5. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined). Rationale: The experiment is a picture–word interference/Stroop-like task probing conflict processing, attention, motivation, and expectancy; it does not involve problem solving processes such as goal-directed planning, sequencing actions to derive a previously unknown solution, or critical-evaluative operations to reach a correct solution. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude because I5 is not satisfied.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (study includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses including healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space: e.g., IPL peaks), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task is a semantic association/retrieval task (SORT) requiring judgment whether word pairs evoke a third object, which indexes semantic retrieval/association rather than goal-directed problem-solving as defined by the review (planning, sequencing, evaluating and executing operations to reach/derive a novel correct solution)). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because the task does not meet the review's problem-solving definition.

This is an fMRI connectivity study of a stop-signal (response inhibition) task using ROI-based Bayesian network analyses in healthy adults. Exclusion criterion E3 applies: the study reports only ROI-based connectivity results rather than whole-brain voxelwise/task-based activation maps. Inclusion criterion I8 is met (study uses BOLD fMRI data). However it does not meet I5 (task is response inhibition, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level whole-brain analysis reported), and I7 (no stereotactic coordinate tables/voxelwise activation coordinates reported). Therefore it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is a PET study with whole-brain, voxelwise rCBF analyses in healthy older adults and reports stereotactic coordinates, but the experimental task (delayed non-match-to-sample) is a working memory/verbal recognition task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence of planning, sequencing, or rule-based problem-solving to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study uses a task probing auditory cognitive control (dichotic listening) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluating, planning/sequencing actions and executing operations to arrive at a solution). Therefore I5 is not met. The manuscript does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion reason: does not meet I5 (task domain mismatch).

This is an fMRI study of semantic selection/semantic priming (metaphors, homonyms, grammatical class) and does not study problem solving as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem-solving/planning/executive operations to arrive at a novel solution). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task as defined), I7 (stereotactic coordinates not explicitly reported in the provided text), I9 (coordinate tables/figures not clearly available in the supplied full text). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED primarily because I5 is not satisfied.

The study does not meet the core review objective criterion I5: although it is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain BOLD analyses and stereotactic results (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the experimental task is a verbal working memory maintenance/manipulation paradigm (recall and sequence reversal) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing/critical evaluation to arrive at a novel solution within semantic, algebraic, logical or mechanical rule frameworks). The task involves memory encoding, rehearsal, and retrieval operations, not higher-order problem solving or critical-thinking operations targeted by the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion IDs met: none.

This study used task-based BOLD fMRI of a virtual radial arm maze requiring goal-directed navigation, memory, planning and decision-making (meets I5). It reports BOLD analyses (meets I8) in healthy adult participants. However, all reported analyses are ROI-based multivariate results rather than whole-brain voxelwise, group-level stereotactic coordinate results. It does not present whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses nor report activation coordinates in Talairach/MNI space, thus failing I6 and I7. Because the paper reports only ROI results, exclusion criterion E3 is met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports a task (probabilistic reversal learning) in healthy adults that requires a goal (choose correct stimulus) and adaptive strategy/planning in response to changing contingencies, fitting the review's operational definition of problem-solving (evaluation of feedback, planning/sequencing a strategy change, executing rule-based choices). It uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses in healthy adults, reports MNI coordinates, and analyzes BOLD responses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, patient-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and is INCLUDED for the review.

This study is an empirical, task-based fMRI/ERP investigation of spatial mental imagery (mental image scanning) in healthy adults. It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) normalization and presents voxelwise results, satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5): the task involves imagining and scanning a learned spatial layout and responding when an imagined object arrives, rather than engaging participants in goal-directed problem solving that requires identifying/planning a sequence of operations to reach a previously unknown solution. Therefore I5 is not met and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations to arrive at a solution). Instead, it investigates event simulation, situational inference, and future-prediction processes. The full text meets other inclusion criteria: I6 (task-based whole-brain fMRI with group-level analysis in healthy adults, N=20), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failure to satisfy I5.

Excluded because the task is a simple perceptual estimation of dot number rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/critical thinking to derive a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per provided definition), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates shown in the provided full text), I9 (no clear reporting of coordinates in main text or accessible supplementary material within the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an fMRI investigation of semantic memory/semantic judgments (same/different color or shape of word pairs). While it includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with MNI coordinates, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) of task-related activations, which fails inclusion criterion I7. The paper does satisfy that it uses a task-based semantic decision paradigm consistent with a semantic problem-solving framework (I5), includes whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults (I6), and reports BOLD-based functional connectivity analyses (I8). However, it does not provide coordinates (I7) and does not provide stereotactic voxelwise coordinate results in text/tables/supplementary materials (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. The study uses task-based whole-brain fMRI and reports group-level effects including healthy adult controls, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analyses. However, the experimental task is a visual attention/multiple-object tracking paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to reach a novel solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it fails to meet I5 while meeting I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using the Tower of London (a problem-solving/planning task) and includes healthy adult controls, seed-based whole-brain functional connectivity analyses, and BOLD measures. These satisfy I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses including healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD fMRI). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (MNI or Talairach) for task-related increases/peaks in the results text/tables supplied; only the MPFC seed coordinate is given. Because reporting of task-related stereotactic coordinates (I7) is not present in the provided content, the study fails to meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study does not examine problem-solving tasks as defined in the review. It investigates spontaneous thought and offline memory reprocessing (resting-state and a memory-recall condition) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing operations to reach an external goal or apply rule-based problem solving. The paper does satisfy several technical criteria (whole-brain group-level BOLD fMRI analysis in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates), but it fails inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD effects with MNI coordinates, the experimental task is a 3-back working memory paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed generation/evaluation/planning to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. It does meet I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI BOLD study with whole-brain, group-level analyses reporting stereotactic (MNI) coordinates in healthy adults (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the task is a moral decision-making paradigm about whether to lie (harmful vs helpful lies) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-oriented planning/sequencing to derive a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reporting, not a non-empirical paper, etc.). Full text appears complete.

This is a PET study of the Stroop color-word task (attention/interference/cognitive control), not a problem-solving task as defined in I5. Explicitly: inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain PET analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (reports rCBF/PET analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is Stroop selective-attention/inhibition, not goal-directed problem solving/planning/sequencing to find a solution), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not reported in the provided full text), and I9 (voxelwise coordinate tables/figures with coordinates are not clearly provided in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy the core problem-solving task definition (I5) and lacks clear stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7/I9).

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed, evaluation/planning/sequencing to reach a solution). The fMRI tasks are simple reaction-time visual checkerboard tasks (sensory/RT), not problem-solving. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/MNI), I8 (reports BOLD and CBF analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review). The tasks used are spatial learning, viewpoint-shift and path-integration training and memory-based virtual maze encoding/retrieval; these are spatial memory/navigation tasks rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a novel solution under a delimited rule set. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of problem-solving task activations.

The study uses a 2-back working memory task in adolescents with schizophrenia and healthy adolescent controls; this is not a problem-solving task as defined (fails I5). Participants are adolescents and include patients, so it does not provide group-level task effects in healthy adults (fails I6). Although the study uses whole-brain BOLD fMRI (I8 satisfied) and reports regional results, it does not meet the core population and task requirements for this review. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper focuses on patient–control comparisons and does not provide the healthy adult task effects required for inclusion. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based PET study using a virtual maze that meets the operational definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed navigation, planning/sequencing, trial-and-error: I5) and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and FDG rCMRglc analyses (satisfying I7, I8, and I9), it does NOT meet the requirement that participants be healthy adult individuals (I6). Participants are regular marijuana users who meet DSM-IV criteria for marijuana dependence and no healthy control group is tested. Thus the study fails the healthy-sample inclusion criterion for the meta-analysis. Applicable exclusion criterion: E5 (study does not include any healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This study examines declarative memory encoding (levels-of-processing semantic vs. shallow tasks) in schizophrenia patients and healthy controls, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (contains group-level whole-brain fMRI effects for healthy adult controls) and I8 (reports BOLD/fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is memory encoding, not problem-solving), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not reported in the provided full text), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures or clear coordinate reporting available in the provided content). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet the critical I5 requirement for problem-solving tasks.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by inclusion criterion I5. The cognitive task used (RSVP target-detection) is an attention/perceptual task, not a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning, sequencing, or rule-based solution generation. The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment used semantic judgment (true/false about single-sentence attributes) to probe semantic memory, which is a recognition/semantic retrieval task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning, sequencing, or executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, no patient-only contrasts, and this is empirical data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses a reward-based instrumental learning task (visual cues and auditory feedback) focused on credit assignment and reward outcome signalling in sensory cortex, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem formulation/critical thinking/planning/sequencing operations to arrive at novel solutions). Additionally, the fMRI acquisition was a partial-volume (48 mm) coverage targeted at visual cortex and reward-related regions rather than whole-brain coverage; thus it does not include a whole-brain group-level analysis as required. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain analysis/group-level whole-brain effects). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly applicable.

This study used a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI Stroop interference task in healthy adult participants (non-manifesting G2019S carriers and non-carriers), with group-level whole-brain analyses reported in Talairach space and functional connectivity/BOLD results. However, the Stroop interference task assesses attention, interference resolution and response inhibition rather than the paper’s meta-analysis definition of problem-solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (problem solving task). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria from the list are met.

This study does not meet I5: the fMRI task is passive speech comprehension (language processing), not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a solution). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses including a healthy elder group), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates, e.g., x: -54,21,24), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because key inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied.

The study uses a task-based BOLD fMRI PVSAT paradigm (subjects perform serial addition rules) which meets the review's problem-solving definition (execution of arithmetic operations according to a rule set). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activations for healthy controls (one-sample t-tests) and between-group random-effects analyses. Images were normalized to MNI space and activation peak coordinates are reported, and BOLD fMRI was used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusion, so content is complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study employed task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI in healthy adults performing a virtual maze spatial-learning task that required goal-directed inference of relative positions (planning/sequencing of spatial relations), satisfying the review's definition of problem-solving in a spatial domain. Group-level whole-brain analyses were performed and reported using MNI space; voxelwise results and statistical maps (with ROI and whole-brain corrections) and BOLD analyses are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a language ambiguity-resolution/semantic decision (homonym matching; yes/no responses) rather than a problem-solving paradigm involving goal-directed planning, sequencing or execution of operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/tabled). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not fit the specified problem-solving definition). No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Although this study meets I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported), it does NOT meet I5. The task is prototype-distortion category learning (classification with feedback) focused on perceptual/category learning and memory processes rather than goal-directed problem solving as defined (planning/sequencing/executive problem-solving operations to reach a solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failure to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task definition).

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task used is a 6-armed bandit reinforcement-learning/explore–exploit decision-making paradigm, which assesses reward-driven choice and exploration/exploitation trade-offs rather than explicit problem solving requiring goal-directed planning, rule-based operations, or critical-evaluative sequencing as defined by I5. The full text meets other imaging-related inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analyses with BOLD fMRI and stereotactic coordinates), but it does not satisfy the core conceptual inclusion criterion of a problem-solving task. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adults (Talairach normalization reported) and associated coordinate results, but it does not investigate problem solving as defined by the review. The tasks are perceptual/semantic action-observation judgments (space: orientation matching; function: compatibility of tool and object) rather than goal-directed problem-solving that requires planning/sequencing or discovering solutions. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT), an affective decision-making task, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-based operations to arrive at a correct/novel solution). It does meet several methodological inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), and the text indicates voxelwise results/cluster tables/figures are available (I9). However, the core content does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving task). Additionally, stereotactic coordinates (I7) are not explicitly provided in the supplied text (tables referenced but coordinates not shown). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5 (and I7 is not demonstrably satisfied in the provided material).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of decision-making/Iowa Gambling Task in Parkinson’s patients and healthy controls, but it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (no goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a correct solution). The paper does include whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults (I6) and reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases in standardized space (MNI/Talairach) for the reported results (I7 not met from the provided content), nor are coordinate tables/figures with results available in the supplied text (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria were directly triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5 (primary conceptual eligibility) and does not provide necessary coordinate reporting in the supplied text (I7/I9).

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The fMRI paradigm assesses moral judgment (decision-making about hypothetical moral dilemmas), which does not clearly require goal-directed problem solving as defined (identifying/planning/sequencing operations within a rule-based framework to arrive at a solution). Criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level task fMRI including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, not purely between-group contrasts, empirical human data present). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study of semantic/word-association (post-lexical semantic relatedness judgments). It includes whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults, reports stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, and BOLD results. However, it does NOT meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): the task is a semantic relatedness/lexical decision, not a goal-directed problem-solving activity involving planning, sequencing, or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of criterial classification and decision-rule effects during memory and perceptual classification tasks (forced-choice, same-different, independent-classification). While it meets neuroimaging methodological criteria (whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates, BOLD fMRI analyses), it does not examine 'problem solving' as defined by the review (a goal-directed task requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution or critical-thinking operations to generate/execute a solution strategy). Instead, the tasks are stimulus classification/judgment problems rather than planning or sequencing actions to solve a previously unknown problem. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is a task-based PET investigation of decision-making (exploration/exploitation) using a stochastic gambling task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-driven critical thinking/planning/sequencing within a rule framework to reach a correct or novel solution). Although it meets neuroimaging criteria (whole-brain group-level PET rCBF analyses reported with stereotactic coordinates), it does not examine problem-solving across domains. Full text appears complete.

The study includes a Tower of London planning task that meets the review’s definition of problem-solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing of moves to reach a target). It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants, with images normalized to MNI space and lists of significant clusters (coordinate results) provided. Voxelwise SPM results are reported and available in figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is mental rotation / perspective-taking, a visuospatial transformation task, but does not meet the review's defined "problem-solving" requirement involving planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). This PET study reports whole-brain, task-based imaging in healthy adults performing a stochastic reversal learning task that is goal-directed (maximize reward) and requires identification and adaptation of stimulus–outcome contingencies (i.e., evaluation, planning/adjustment of actions, and execution to obtain reward), which fits the provided definition of a problem-solving task. The study used group-level whole-brain rCBF analyses (SPM) in healthy adult participants, reported task-related rCBF results, and indicates voxelwise analyses with reported activation clusters (results presented via contrasts and correlation maps; figures/tables referenced). Thus it meets I5 (goal-directed adaptive problem-solving/reversal learning), I6 (group whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (voxelwise stereotactic results reported/available in figures/tables), I8 (rCBF PET analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a methods paper applying a group network detection algorithm to fMRI data collected during a motor tracking/squeezing task, not a problem-solving task. Exclusion reasons: E3 (reports only ROI-based results). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (uses BOLD fMRI). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task is motor tracking, not defined problem-solving as per review), I6 (does not perform a whole-brain voxelwise group analysis; uses anatomically defined ROIs), I7 (does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s scope and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (fixed-effects across N=5), uses BOLD contrast maps in MNI space, and reports activation maps/tables, but the experimental task is a visual checkerboard with attentional modulation (attend/ignore/discriminate). It does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing or rule-based solution processes such as semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical tasks). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a non-empirical commentary/review (Exclusion E6). It does not report original task-based fMRI or PET experiment data in healthy adults: no methods, participant details, task design, group-level whole-brain analyses, stereotactic coordinates, or BOLD/rCBF results are presented. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analyses reported), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results provided). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating probabilistic prediction/uncertainty and learning, but it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal-directed task requiring critical evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to arrive at a (previously unknown) solution). The task here involves predicting which of two figures will 'win' based on learned probabilities—this is decision-making/probabilistic learning rather than problem solving per the I5 definition. The paper meets whole-brain, group-level BOLD analysis requirements (I6, I8) but does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving paradigm). Also, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables/explicit coordinates in Talairach/MNI space in the text excerpt supplied, so I7 cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Outcome: EXCLUDE because I5 not met (and I7 unconfirmed).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study of contingency learning/reversal learning and executive control, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinate results in tables/figures), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the experimental task is a two-alternative choice/reversal-learning paradigm examining contingency detection, valuation, and updating (win-stay/lose-shift behavior and responses to value/effect changes), rather than a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning, critical evaluation, sequencing of actions to reach a novel solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failure to meet I5.

This study was excluded because it does not meet the review’s core problem-solving task requirement (I5). The fMRI task is a dual-task letter/number discrimination paradigm measuring executive function/dual-task processing (maintenance, coordination, response selection, conflict monitoring) rather than a problem-solving task entailing a goal, planning/sequencing operations, or deriving a previously unknown solution within a delimited rule set. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined). I7 (stereotactic coordinates) likely reported in tables but are not explicit in the provided text; however, this uncertainty does not change exclusion because I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I5: the in-scanner task is a Go/No Go response-inhibition/attention task, which does not qualify as a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/operations to arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain fMRI with group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6). Full text appears complete and contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is a theory-of-mind (ToM) moving-shapes paradigm assessing social cognition/mentalizing, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem identification, planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not involve problem-solving as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the review definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The modified rock–paper–scissors paradigm is an inhibition-of-stereotyped-response task (attempting to ‘lose’ vs. ‘win’) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing, and execution to arrive at a novel/appropriate solution as defined in I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is an inhibitory response task, not a problem-solving task per the review definition). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore EXCLUDE due to failure to satisfy I5.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis’ definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task used (POP, a Stroop-derived cognitive-control/conflict task) probes executive control/preparation and conflict monitoring rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a (previously unknown) solution. While the study includes whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with group-level effects in elderly healthy comparison participants (I6) and reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), it does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases in the main text or tables accessible here (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results in MNI space and provides coordinate tables; however, the experimental task is a delayed-encoding recognition/manipulation paradigm (chunking, segmenting, binding) testing working memory and sequencing of prelearned items rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed search for a solution or planning/executive problem solving to arrive at a novel or discovered solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Detailed summary: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (does not evaluate a problem-solving task as defined). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is a whole‑brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting group-level BOLD effects and stereotactic coordinates (MNI), it does not investigate problem‑solving as defined in the review (I5). The tasks are social judgements (approachability and perceived intelligence from faces), involving binary evaluative decisions, not goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing actions, or executing operations within a rule set to reach a solution. Therefore I5 is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This task-based fMRI study involves goal-directed decision-making and planning (e.g., deciding when to execute left turns with oncoming traffic under traffic rules and performing secondary cognitive tasks while driving), fulfilling the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (16 young drivers) using BOLD fMRI (I6,I8). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space and shown in tables/figures (I7,I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), contain healthy-group task effects, and are empirical. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using the sugar production factory (SPF) paradigm, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (explicit goal, need to figure out actions to reach a target and adjust strategy across trials). The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (inter-subject t-tests) with BOLD contrasts pre- and post-training and uses stereotactic atlases (Talairach Daemon/WFU_Pickatlas) to report anatomical loci; task-related activations and learning-related increases/decreases are described and implied to be reported in standardized coordinate space/tables/figures. ROI analyses are supplementary and the paper does not rely solely on ROI results. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and the study should be included.

This study uses an N-back working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem formulation, planning/sequencing to derive a novel solution). While it does report whole-brain BOLD fMRI results in stereotactic (Talairach) space and includes healthy adult comparison subjects, it does not meet the required definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses with healthy adult participants), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is working memory N-back, not problem solving). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment that examines semantic event sequencing—a sequencing/planning executive task consistent with the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning and sequencing). It reports whole-brain, group-level within-group effects for healthy adult controls and between-group contrasts, with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and voxelwise BOLD results. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9. Full text content is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses an n-back working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence the task required goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution). It does meet other required criteria: I6 (includes healthy adult group-level whole-brain analyses and within-group task effects in controls), I7 (reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results presented in figures and text). No exclusion criteria are triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults studying cognitive control, working memory, and target detection/switching, not a problem-solving task as defined in the review (no goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a solution across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results indicated as available). This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met) and the neuroimaging analysis is ROI-based rather than a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis (E3; I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/MNI results), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/SVC results reported in tables/figures). This PET study reports whole-brain, group-level rCBF analyses (SPM) in healthy adult participants using Talairach coordinates and presents voxelwise task-related effects across the brain.
